recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. It is nestled amidst a vibrant bed of roasted bell pepper strips, cut into uniform 2cm batons, in shades of rich red and sunny yellow. The bell peppers are glistening with a rustic tomato-herb sauce, showing gentle charring from sautéing. A crisp, golden-brown crust of melted Parmesan cheese generously covers the chicken and parts of the bell peppers, offering a textural contrast. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a bright color pop. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even. A fork and knife, traditional flatware, are placed on either side of the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium heat.
Add bell pepper strips. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and slightly charred. Remove from pan.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Return bell peppers to the pan with the tomato sauce. Stir in half of the fresh basil.
Place seared chicken breasts into the sauce in the pan. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese generously over the chicken and bell pepper mixture.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and Parmesan is golden and bubbly.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Vegetable Barley Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of Spicy Chicken and Vegetable Barley Skillet is presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with subtle imperfections, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features generous chunks of seared chicken breast (approximately 3cm cubes) nestled among plump, toothsome barley grains. Brightly colored diced bell peppers (red and yellow), diced carrots, and vibrant green peas are interspersed throughout, creating a visually appealing medley of textures and natural hues. The rich, savory tomato-based sauce lightly coats all ingredients, giving a comforting sheen. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a final touch of verdant freshness. The plate is adequately filled, allowing for some negative space. Standard flatware is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a relaxed family meal.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3 cm chunks. Dice onion, red and yellow bell peppers, and carrots. Finely chop chili. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion, bell peppers, carrots, and chopped chili to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and pearl barley to the skillet. Stir well.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until barley is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Add frozen green peas. Stir and cook for another 5 minutes, or until chicken is heated through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish individual servings with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
For a lower calorie option, ensure to use lean chicken breast and measure olive oil precisely.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef and Bell Pepper Pörkölt
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rich, dark red Hungarian Beef Pörkölt is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender, braised beef chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled amongst vibrant, softened bell pepper chunks (2 cm), caramelized onions, and a thick, glossy paprika-infused sauce. The beef exhibits a deep, browned crust from initial searing and a fork-tender interior. The bell peppers retain their distinct colors – crimson red, sunny yellow, and forest green – providing visual contrast against the stew's deep hue. A small dollop of sour cream or crème fraîche is gently swirled on top, offering a creamy counterpoint. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley. Beside the bowl, a slice of crusty artisan bread or a small portion of nokedli (Hungarian dumplings) is arranged on a simple white porcelain plate, inviting a complete experience, set on a simple wooden table with natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian egg noodles/dumplings), boiled potatoes, or crusty bread.
Traditionally accompanied by a side of pickled cucumbers or pickled cabbage.
Often served with a dollop of sour cream (tejföl) on top.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck or stewing beef, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Bell peppers (mixed colors), deseeded and cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and crushed caraway seeds. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in Hungarian paprika quickly to prevent burning.
Return beef to the pot. Stir well to coat beef with paprika and onions.
Add diced bell peppers, diced tomatoes, and beef broth. Stir in Dijon mustard and dried marjoram.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
If desired, mix 1 tablespoon flour with 2 tablespoons water to create a slurry. Stir into the simmering stew during the last 30 minutes of cooking to slightly thicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality Hungarian sweet paprika.
The stew tastes even better the next day.
traditional_techniques: Searing meat before braising to develop flavor
Building flavor layers with paprika, onions, and other aromatics

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Chickpea and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Lemon Chickpea and Rice Soup is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a light wooden table. The soup features a vibrant, slightly creamy yellow broth with visible tender white Arborio rice grains, pale golden chickpeas, and soft 1.5 cm diced potatoes. Small pieces of bright red diced tomatoes add color. The surface is garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and delicate dill sprigs, offering a fresh contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. A simple white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's textures and colors, set against a subtle, modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (300 g), peeled, diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, undrained diced tomatoes, rinsed chickpeas, and Arborio rice to the pot.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer 20-25 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Cook until potatoes are tender and rice is cooked through.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in fresh lemon juice.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and dill. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon-Chickpea & Potato Velouté with Crispy Basmati Rice, Herb Oil, and Microgreens
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of luminous, pale yellow velouté rests in an elegant, shallow bone china bowl. The soup's surface is impeccably smooth, reflecting light. A vibrant green herb oil, precisely swirled, creates an artistic contrast against the velouté's creamy hue. Centered atop this, a delicate mound of golden-crisp basmati rice provides textural intrigue, its irregular shapes catching the light. Adjacent, a cluster of fresh, verdant microgreens adds a final touch of living color and height. The bowl sits on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a subtly patterned designer plate and a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting emphasizes the dish's refined simplicity, casting soft shadows that enhance depth, with ample negative space.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potato and cooked chickpeas to the saucepan. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are very tender.

Remove from heat. Blend the soup using an immersion blender until very smooth. Alternatively, transfer to a high-speed blender and blend until silky. Pass the soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan for an ultra-smooth consistency.
Return the sieved velouté to low heat. Stir in lemon zest and lemon juice. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan or deep fryer to 170°C. Carefully add cooled cooked basmati rice in small batches. Fry until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Blanch parsley and chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Squeeze out excess water.
Combine blanched herbs and olive oil in a small blender. Blend until very smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil. Season with a pinch of salt.

Ladle the warm velouté into individual shallow soup bowls. Create a swirl or a few drops of herb oil on the surface of the soup. Carefully place a small mound of crispy basmati rice in the center or slightly off-center. Garnish with a small cluster of microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: Passing the soup through a sieve is crucial for a fine-dining texture.
Ensure the herb oil is vibrant green; blanching helps maintain color.
Fry rice in small batches to avoid clumping and ensure even crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Apple and Oat Soup with Leek
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, golden-beige soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The soup has a smooth, velvety texture, with a natural sheen. A swirl of bright yellow lemon butter glistens on the surface. Small, finely diced apple pieces are just visible within the creamy base, adding subtle texture. A few fresh green thyme leaves are scattered artfully on top as a simple garnish. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with visible grain and natural imperfections. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, cozy lighting creating a relaxed atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the inviting, comforting appearance of the soup.
instructions: Clean leek thoroughly. Slice white and light green parts into thin rounds.
Dice onion into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Peel, core, and dice apples into small cubes.
Melt 30 g butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add leek and onion. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced apples, gluten-free oats, and brown sugar. Stir well.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes. Oats should be tender.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to purée soup until smooth. Or carefully transfer to a regular blender and blend.
Stir in milk. Return pot to low heat. Heat through gently, do not boil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small pan, melt remaining 20 g butter. Add juice of half a lemon. Stir.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Drizzle each serving with lemon butter. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves or a sprinkle of black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Lemon Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, off-white ceramic bowl, showcasing its fluid, 'all'onda' consistency. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded generously with substantial, pan-roasted cremini mushroom slices, their deep brown caps providing a striking contrast. Finely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the top, adding vibrant green flecks and a fresh aroma. The rice grains are plump and distinct, enveloped in a luscious, velvety sauce. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, inviting and comforting. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple linen napkin and a traditional Italian-style spoon. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene from above, highlighting the risotto's inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Often accompanied by a glass of crisp white wine.
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a separate pot. Keep it hot.
Clean and slice mushrooms into 0.5 cm thick pieces.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, melt 30 g butter with 15 ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges become translucent.
Pour in 120 ml hot vegetable broth. Stir until almost fully absorbed.
Continue adding hot broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir frequently. Allow each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and 'al dente' (firm to the bite) when done.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter, grated Parmesan cheese, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Add roasted mushrooms and most of the chopped parsley. Stir gently to combine.
Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: For the best texture, use a good quality Arborio rice.
Ensure the vegetable broth is always hot before adding to the risotto.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Soy-Ginger Glaze, Sautéed Broccoli, and Quinoa
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A pan-seared duck breast, with its skin rendered to a crisp, golden-brown, is the focal point, resting as a whole piece or a thick half. Its interior reveals a rich, rosy medium-rare hue. Beside the duck, a neat mound of fluffy, white quinoa forms a comforting base. Vibrant green, tender-crisp blanched and sautéed broccoli florets are artfully arranged around the duck and quinoa, adding color and texture. A glistening, savory soy-ginger glaze lightly coats the duck and is drizzled sparingly over the plate. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation. A set of simple dark chopsticks rests beside the plate, with a small, empty rice bowl for optional extra rice in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served individually on a plate with optional side of steamed rice in a small bowl, and chopsticks.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Combine quinoa with 400 ml water or broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Let stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Score the duck breast skin in a crisscross pattern, without cutting into the meat. Season duck breasts liberally with salt and black pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, honey (or maple syrup), rice vinegar, and sesame oil to create the glaze.

Cut broccoli into small florets. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 2-3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking, then drain well.

Heat a heavy-bottomed pan (preferably cast iron) over medium-high heat. Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in the cold pan. Cook for 8-10 minutes, allowing the fat to render and the skin to become crispy and golden brown. Pour off rendered fat as it accumulates.

Flip duck breasts and sear for another 3-5 minutes for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare. Transfer duck to a cutting board and let rest for 5 minutes.

While duck rests, add 5 ml vegetable oil to the same pan (or a clean pan). Add blanched broccoli florets and sauté for 2-3 minutes until heated through and slightly charred. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the prepared soy-ginger glaze to the pan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until slightly thickened. Slice the rested duck breasts into thick, even pieces or halve them.

To plate, place a mound of fluffy quinoa on each plate. Arrange the sliced duck breast beside the quinoa. Place sautéed broccoli florets around the duck and quinoa. Drizzle the warm soy-ginger glaze over the duck and broccoli. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure duck breast is cooked to desired doneness, typically medium-rare to medium for optimal texture. Rest duck properly before slicing to retain juices.
Rendered duck fat can be saved and used for cooking vegetables or potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Charred Broccoli and Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned. The duck breast, cut into two or three thick, succulent pieces, showcases a perfectly crisp, golden-brown skin with visible crosshatch scoring, contrasting with the rosy, tender interior of the meat. Beside the duck, vibrant green broccoli florets are artfully arranged, exhibiting delightful charring on their edges and tips, indicating a tender-crisp texture. A rich, glossy, deep mahogany red wine jus is elegantly drizzled over the duck and lightly pooled at its base, adding a sophisticated sheen. A small sprig of fresh thyme rests on the duck, providing a subtle pop of color and aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, with a soft, casually elegant restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple potato gratin or roasted potatoes.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Pinot Noir or Merlot.
instructions: Score the skin of each duck breast in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into the meat.
Season duck breasts generously with salt and black pepper.
Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in a cold, oven-safe pan. Cook over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes. Render the fat slowly until skin is golden and crisp.
Pour off excess rendered fat. Flip duck breasts. Sear meat-side down for 3-4 minutes for medium-rare.
Transfer the pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes to finish cooking. (Internal temperature for duck is typically 60-65°C for medium-rare, adjust to preference).
Remove duck from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes, covered loosely with foil.
While duck rests, prepare broccoli. Cut broccoli into small florets. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a separate pan over high heat. Add blanched broccoli. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until charred and tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
For the jus: Pour off most duck fat from the pan used for duck, leaving 15ml. Add diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Deglaze the pan with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken or duck stock. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, reducing until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat. Whisk in 30g cold butter, one piece at a time, until smooth and glossy. Season jus with salt and pepper.
Slice each duck breast into 2-3 thick pieces (not fanned).
Arrange charred broccoli on serving plates. Place duck breast pieces beside broccoli. Spoon red wine jus over the duck. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Resting the duck after cooking is crucial for juicy, tender meat.
Render the duck fat slowly over low heat to achieve maximum crispness on the skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Quinoa Loaf Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, clean slice of Lemon Quinoa Loaf Cake rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice is pale yellow with visible flecks of lemon zest and small, soft quinoa grains embedded in its moist crumb. A thin, translucent white lemon glaze cascades gently over the top of the slice, pooling slightly at the base. In the background, the remaining loaf cake sits on a simple wooden cutting board. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a simple fork beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's inviting texture. The arrangement is natural and unfussy, evoking a relaxed family dining atmosphere with minimal, unobtrusive clutter in the background.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Combine quinoa and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer covered for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and lightly flour a 900g loaf pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, caster sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk eggs, milk, vegetable oil, lemon zest, and 30 ml lemon juice until well combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in the cooked quinoa.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. The internal temperature should be above 90°C.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
While the cake cools, prepare the glaze. Whisk icing sugar and 50 ml lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth.
Once the cake is completely cool, pour the lemon glaze over the top. Let the glaze set before slicing and serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano con Arroz Rojo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally featuring two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply coated in a rich, velvety mole poblano sauce. The chicken, cooked to tender perfection, exhibits a dark, glossy, reddish-brown hue from the mole. A generous mound of vibrant, reddish-orange Arroz Rojo, fluffy and perfectly cooked, sits beside the chicken, speckled with finely diced onion. The plate is garnished simply yet authentically: a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds over the mole, a fresh lime wedge, and a small cluster of finely chopped white onion. A cotton napkin is placed to the side on a simple wooden table. Natural, even lighting highlights the food’s textures and colors. A traditional Mexican ceramic bowl for accompaniments completes the modern bistro setting. The composition is balanced, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Lime wedges
Finely chopped white onion
Toasted sesame seeds

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.quantity: 1.5 litres (1 litre for mole, 500 ml for rice)

instructions: Prepare chiles: Remove stems and seeds from ancho, mulato, and pasilla chiles. Lightly toast chiles on a dry comal or pan until fragrant. Rehydrate in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast nuts, seeds, and spices: In a dry pan, toast sesame seeds, almonds, peanuts, cinnamon stick, whole cloves, star anise, coriander seeds, and cumin. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Heat 15 ml lard/oil in a pan. Sauté 1 medium chopped onion, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 medium tomatoes, and 2 medium tomatillos until softened. Add dried thyme and Mexican oregano.

Blend mole ingredients: Drain rehydrated chiles. Combine chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, sautéed aromatics, stale bread/tortilla, and 250 ml chicken broth in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids.

Cook mole sauce: Heat 30 ml lard/oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour in the strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 15-20 minutes until it darkens and thickens significantly.

Add chocolate and broth: Stir in dark chocolate until melted. Gradually add remaining 750 ml chicken broth, stirring until smooth. Season with salt and optional sugar. Simmer mole gently for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook chicken: Season chicken thighs with salt. Heat 15 ml lard/oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear other side.
Finish chicken in mole: Add seared chicken to the simmering mole sauce. Ensure chicken is submerged. Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Prepare arroz rojo: Heat 15 ml oil in a medium saucepan. Sauté 1/2 small diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves until fragrant. Add 300 g rinsed long-grain rice. Sauté until lightly toasted.
Add tomato and broth to rice: Stir in 200 ml tomato puree. Add 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 18 minutes. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
traditional_techniques: Fritura de Mole (Frying the Mole Paste)

recipes.recipe_name: 7 Up Braised Chicken Thighs with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust portion of 7 Up Braised Chicken Thighs is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A whole, golden-brown chicken thigh, its skin crisply rendered, sits prominently at the center. A rich, amber-hued, glossy sauce is generously spooned over the chicken and pooled around its base. Alongside, three to four thick batons of roasted carrots and parsnips, displaying caramelized edges and vibrant colors, are artfully arranged. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard polished flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, with a casual restaurant background subtly blurred to maintain focus on the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Cut carrots and parsnips into thick batons. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelized.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in 7 Up, chicken broth, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pot and keep warm. Place the pot back on the stovetop over medium heat. Skim any excess fat from the sauce.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water to create a slurry. Slowly whisk slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve chicken thighs with the thickened sauce and roasted root vegetables. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Rockfish with Tomato-Olive Vinaigrette and Sautéed Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: The pan-seared rockfish is presented as a whole, golden-brown fillet, its crispy skin or lightly seared surface contrasting with the vibrant components. It rests atop a modest bed of sautéed Swiss chard, its deep green leaves gently wilted and intertwined. A generous spoonful of bright, colorful tomato-olive vinaigrette cascades over the fish, showcasing small cubes of red bell pepper, finely diced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, and roughly chopped Kalamata olives, all studded with finely chopped fresh dill. The vinaigrette adds pops of red, green, and dark purple against the flaky white fish and dark green chard. The dish is served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, leaving ample negative space. A fresh lemon wedge is placed alongside the fish. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and fresh colors of the ingredients, focusing entirely on the single, refined portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lemon wedges.
Accompany with crusty bread like baguette or focaccia to soak up the vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat rockfish fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Dice red bell pepper into small 5mm cubes. Mince 2 cloves garlic. Finely dice red onion. Halve cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop pitted Kalamata olives. Finely chop fresh dill.

Combine bell pepper, minced garlic, red onion, cherry tomatoes, olives, and dill in a bowl. Add 30 ml olive oil and juice from half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well to create the vinaigrette.
Wash Swiss chard. Remove thick stems. Chop leaves into 2 cm strips. Mince remaining 2 cloves garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add Swiss chard to the pan. Sauté 3-5 minutes until wilted and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place rockfish fillets skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down. Sear 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
Flip fillets. Sear another 3-4 minutes until cooked through and flaky. Internal temperature should reach 63°C.
Place a bed of sautéed Swiss chard on each plate. Top with a seared rockfish fillet. Spoon generous amount of tomato-olive vinaigrette over the fish.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.
notes: Rockfish is a lean, firm white fish. Adjust cooking time based on fillet thickness.

recipes.recipe_name: Vitello Scaloppine al Rosmarino e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three golden-brown seared veal medallions are arranged slightly overlapping in the center. They are coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, clinging lightly to the meat. The sauce is speckled with finely chopped fresh parsley, adding a bright green contrast. A small, fresh rosemary sprig is placed artfully on top of one medallion as a garnish. The veal is tender, showcasing its natural texture. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the dish to breathe. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface. Traditional Italian flatware is neatly placed beside the plate. A small, rustic piece of crusty artisan bread and a small dish of seasoned olive oil are positioned to the side. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The focus remains on the food, highlighting its appealing colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Place veal cutlets between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound gently with a mallet until 5 mm thick.
Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear veal cutlets in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic, dried chili flakes, and 1 sprig of rosemary (leaves stripped and chopped) to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return seared veal cutlets to the pan. Ensure they are coated in sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, ensuring veal is cooked through (internal temperature 70-75°C).
Finely chop fresh parsley. Stir half of the chopped parsley into the sauce.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and a small sprig of fresh rosemary.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Swordfish with Creamy Tomato-Garlic Sauce and Lemon Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick, pan-seared swordfish steak, golden-brown with a delicate crust, rests atop a bed of fluffy white lemon rice. The swordfish is presented as a whole piece. A vibrant, creamy reddish-orange tomato-garlic sauce generously cascades over the swordfish and pools around the rice. The sauce exhibits small, tender diced tomato pieces and hints of minced garlic. Bright green chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the dish, with a fresh lemon wedge placed beside the swordfish for an accent of color and freshness. The dish is served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin nearby, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting. The plating is clean, organized, and professional with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 500ml water or broth and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
While rice cooks, pat swordfish steaks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear swordfish steaks for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove swordfish from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the same pan. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry vermouth, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes, reducing liquid slightly.
Stir in diced tomatoes and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in lemon juice. Keep warm.
Fluff cooked rice. Stir in lemon zest and half of the chopped parsley.

To serve, place a portion of lemon rice on each plate. Top with a seared swordfish steak. Spoon generous amounts of creamy tomato-garlic sauce over the swordfish. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is served on a wide, flat white porcelain plate. The consistency is fluid and free-flowing, spreading naturally across the dish in the traditional all'onda style. The rice grains are plump, glossy, and distinct. Thick, meaty chunks of golden-brown sautéed mushrooms are distributed throughout the rice. The color palette features creamy whites, earthy browns, and soft golds. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano and tiny green thyme leaves garnish the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with clean margins. Soft natural side lighting emphasizes the creamy emulsion. The background shows a modern bistro setting with a light oak table and a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on flat plates to allow the risotto to spread.
Pair with a dry Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio.
Provide a high-quality silver spoon for dining.
Serve immediately while the rice maintains its fluid texture.
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a pot. Keep at a low simmer.
Clean mushrooms. Cut into 2cm chunks.
Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until browned. Season with salt. Remove and set aside.
Finely dice shallots.
Melt 30g butter in a heavy pan. Add shallots. Cook until translucent.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly.
Add more stock only after the previous ladle is absorbed.
Fold in sautéed mushrooms after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente, approximately 18 minutes total.
Remove from heat. Add remaining butter and Parmigiano Reggiano.
Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion. This is mantecatura.
Adjust consistency with a final splash of stock. The risotto must be fluid.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Never wash the rice; the surface starch is essential for creaminess.
Ensure the stock is hot to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.
The final texture should be 'all'onda', meaning it moves like a wave when the plate is tilted.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Herbed Quinoa and Steamed Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared duck breast, with beautifully rendered, golden-brown crispy skin and a tender, rosy pink interior, is the focal point. It rests slightly off-center on a simple, round ceramic plate. Beside the duck, a generous, fluffy mound of herbed quinoa, flecked with bright green parsley and thyme, provides a wholesome base. Around the main components, vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are casually arranged, adding a fresh contrast. The duck is presented as a whole piece or thick halves, showcasing its natural form, not sliced and fanned. The plate is set on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple fork and knife and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the dish, creating an appetizing, home-cooked feel.
instructions: Rinse quinoa under cold water. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced shallot and minced garlic. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add quinoa to the saucepan. Toast 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.
While quinoa cooks, score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into the flesh.
Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in a cold, oven-safe pan. Turn heat to medium-low.
Cook skin-side down for 8-12 minutes. Render fat until skin is crispy and golden brown. Pour off excess fat periodically.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 3-5 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 57-60°C). Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove duck from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Cut broccoli into florets. Steam or boil broccoli until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes.
Fluff quinoa with a fork. Stir in chopped parsley and thyme. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve duck breast whole or cut into thick halves alongside herbed quinoa and steamed broccoli.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Duck Leg with Crispy Potatoes and Quinoa-Broccoli Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted duck leg, skin golden-brown and visibly crispy, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The duck leg is presented whole. Beside it, a cluster of golden-brown roasted potato wedges and chunks shows a rustic texture. A vibrant mound of quinoa-broccoli salad is artfully placed, showcasing bright green 3cm broccoli florets, ruby-red halved cherry tomatoes, small white quinoa, and finely diced red onion. Fresh, roughly chopped parsley is sprinkled over the salad, and a bright yellow lemon wedge is near the duck. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. A cotton napkin and standard flatware are neatly arranged beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread on the side.
Pair with a glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Score duck leg skin in a crisscross pattern. Season with salt and pepper.
Place duck legs skin-side up in a large roasting tray. Roast for 30 minutes.
Wash potatoes. Cut small potatoes into halves, larger ones into quarters.
Finely chop garlic cloves.
After 30 minutes, remove duck from oven. Add potatoes and chopped garlic to the tray. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Toss to coat.
Return tray to oven. Increase temperature to 200°C. Roast for another 40-50 minutes, or until duck skin is crispy and potatoes are tender and golden. Flip potatoes halfway through.
Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water.

Cook quinoa: Combine rinsed quinoa with 400ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Cut broccoli into 3cm florets. Steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes. Immediately plunge into ice water to stop cooking, then drain well.
Finely dice red onion. Halve cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, blanched broccoli, diced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped parsley.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk remaining 30ml olive oil with juice of half a lemon, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over quinoa mixture. Toss gently to combine.

To serve: Place a roasted duck leg on each plate. Arrange crispy potatoes beside the duck. Spoon a generous portion of quinoa-broccoli salad onto the plate. Garnish with a lemon wedge and extra fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Arancini di Riso e Patate al Formaggio
recipes.visual_description: Four golden-brown Arancini di Riso e Patate al Formaggio are neatly arranged on a clean white porcelain plate. Each arancino displays a crispy, textured exterior, approximately 6 cm in diameter. A vibrant red marinara sauce is artfully spooned alongside, creating a contrasting pool of color. Fresh, torn basil leaves are scattered lightly over the sauce and arancini, providing a bright garnish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the rich colors and textures. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin is to the left, with a polished silver fork and knife to the right. A softly blurred background suggests a modern bistro. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's features.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm marinara sauce
Garnish with fresh basil
instructions: In a saucepan, melt 15g butter. Add rice, toast 1 minute. Pour in 100ml broth. Stir until absorbed. Gradually add remaining broth, 100ml at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed. Cook until rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes. Stir in Parmesan, remaining 15g butter, and saffron if using. Season with salt and pepper. Spread rice on a tray. Chill completely for at least 2 hours.
Boil diced potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well. Mash potatoes until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool.

Take a spoonful of chilled rice. Flatten in your palm. Place a small amount of mashed potato in the center. Top with a few pieces of diced mozzarella. Carefully enclose the filling with more rice, forming a ball about 5-6 cm in diameter. Ensure no filling is exposed.

Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs. Roll each arancino first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in egg, ensuring full coating. Finally, roll in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 170°C. Fry arancini in batches, 3-4 at a time, for 5-7 minutes. Turn occasionally until deeply golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature is hot and cheese is melted.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with warm marinara sauce and fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Bean Chili
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of spicy chicken and bean chili is presented in a shallow white ceramic bowl. The rich, dark red chili base is thick and robust, featuring visible chunks of seared chicken thigh (approximately 3cm cubes), vibrant diced red and yellow bell peppers (1.5cm cubes), and plump kidney beans. A dollop of creamy white Mexican crema sits slightly off-center, contrasting beautifully with the chili's deep color. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered artfully over the crema and chili. A bright lime wedge rests on the bowl's rim. The bowl is placed on a rustic wooden table, accompanied by a small basket of warm corn tortillas and a side dish of shredded Monterey Jack cheese. A simple metal fork and spoon are beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Mexican crema or sour cream
Shredded cheese (Cheddar or Monterey Jack)
Fresh lime wedges

ingredients.name: Dried ancho chilies, rehydrated and chopped
Canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained
Fresh red chilies (e.g., serrano), thinly sliced

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in chopped rehydrated ancho chilies, chili powder, cumin, oregano, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rinsed kidney beans, chopped pickled jalapeños, and sliced fresh chilies. Return seared chicken to the pot.
Bring chili to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 60 minutes, or up to 2 hours, stirring occasionally. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro, a dollop of Mexican crema, and a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust the amount of fresh chilies and pickled jalapeños to control the spice level.
For a deeper flavor, let the chili simmer longer, up to 3 hours.
traditional_techniques: Layering flavors with spices and chilies

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Smoked Paprika Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish Smoked Paprika Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Three generous chunks of browned chicken, approximately 3cm each, are nestled amidst golden-orange bomba rice, which is cooked to a fluid consistency. The rice, infused with rich smoked paprika and tender diced tomatoes, shows distinct, al dente grains. Bright green fresh savory leaves are scattered throughout, adding an herbaceous contrast. A single lemon wedge sits on the plate's rim. The dish is placed on a rustic wooden table, accompanied by a simple folded cotton napkin. The setting evokes a modern bistro, illuminated by soft, natural light, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful rice.
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine like Albariño or a light red such as Rioja Crianza.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Dice the onion. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince the garlic. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in bomba rice. Cook for 2 minutes, coating the grains thoroughly.
Add diced tomatoes, half of the fresh savory leaves, and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return the seared chicken chunks to the pot. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low.
Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in the remaining fresh savory leaves. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Let the dish rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve immediately with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Braised Red Cabbage and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden brown and crispy-skinned, rests slightly off-center on a white porcelain plate. It is nestled beside a vibrant mound of deep reddish-purple braised red cabbage, shredded thinly. Scattered around are earthy, caramelized chunks of roasted potato (2 cm cubes) and bright orange carrot rounds (1.5 cm thick). A light drizzle of pan juices from the chicken lightly coats the plate. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley over the chicken and vegetables. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, with traditional German flatware placed alongside the plate. A folded linen napkin completes the clean, natural scene under even, soft lighting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and appealing individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of grainy mustard.
Traditionally accompanied by a glass of German beer or apple juice.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Spread 15 g mustard evenly over chicken.
Peel and chop 1 onion into 2 cm chunks. Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Peel and cut carrots into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Peel and smash 2 garlic cloves.
Toss chopped onion, potatoes, carrots, and smashed garlic with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper in a roasting pan.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on top of vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 30 minutes.
While chicken roasts, prepare red cabbage. Halve and core red cabbage. Shred thinly.
Peel and thinly slice remaining 1 onion. Peel, core, and dice apple into 1 cm cubes. Peel and mince remaining 2 garlic cloves.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add sliced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and diced apple. Sauté 2 minutes.
Add shredded red cabbage and bay leaves. Stir well. Pour in apple cider vinegar and chicken stock. Add remaining 15 g mustard, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until cabbage is tender. Stir occasionally.
After 30 minutes, check chicken. Continue roasting until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden brown and crispy, approximately 15-20 more minutes.
Remove chicken and vegetables from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley.
To serve, plate one chicken thigh. Spoon a generous portion of braised red cabbage alongside. Add roasted potato cubes and carrot rounds. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sweetness of braised cabbage by adding a pinch of sugar if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Eggplant & Sweet Sausage Bruschetta with Honeyed Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant platter of Caramelized Eggplant & Sweet Sausage Bruschetta. Ten to twelve toasted baguette slices, each a golden-brown base, are neatly arranged on a simple white rectangular plate or a light wooden board. Each piece is generously spread with creamy, bright white honeyed ricotta. On top, a colorful medley of deep purple-brown caramelized eggplant cubes, ruby-red roasted cherry tomato halves, and savory, crumbly brown sweet sausage. A delicate drizzle of golden honey glistens over the toppings. Fresh green mint leaves, finely chiffonaded, or small basil leaves provide a final aromatic and visual flourish. The textures are varied: crisp bread, tender eggplant, juicy tomatoes, and creamy cheese. The presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice eggplant into 1 cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté eggplant cubes until tender and deeply caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into the same pan. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
Toss halved cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes, or until softened and slightly burst.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Brush slices with olive oil. Toast in oven for 5-7 minutes until golden.
In a small bowl, combine ricotta, Greek yogurt, and 15 g honey. Whip until smooth and creamy. Season lightly with salt.
Assemble bruschetta: Spread honeyed ricotta generously on each toasted baguette slice. Top with caramelized eggplant, roasted cherry tomatoes, and crumbled sausage.
Drizzle with remaining honey. Garnish each bruschetta with fresh mint or basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek-Style Baked Eggplant with Spiced Sausage and Feta-Yogurt Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous rectangular portion of baked eggplant and sausage is centrally placed on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features distinct, appealing layers: a golden-brown, slightly puffed feta-yogurt topping forms a creamy crust. Beneath, visible softened, caramelized eggplant rounds with their deep purple skins provide a rich backdrop. Between the eggplant, a savory, reddish-brown spiced sausage and tomato mixture peeks through, showcasing its hearty texture. The top is lightly scattered with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The eggplant is cut into 1 cm thick rounds, while onions are finely diced. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and knife resting beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warm colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple Greek salad (horiatiki).
Offer a side of Kalamata olives.

ingredients.name: Eggplant
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (about 600g), sliced into 1 cm thick rounds

instructions: Place eggplant rounds in a colander. Sprinkle heavily with salt. Let drain for 30 minutes. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add eggplant rounds in batches. Cook until golden brown on both sides. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Remove sausage and set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving 1-2 tablespoons.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Return sausage to the pan. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Remove bay leaf.

In a baking dish (approximately 20x30 cm), arrange half of the browned eggplant slices. Spread half of the sausage-tomato mixture over the eggplant. Repeat layers with remaining eggplant and sausage mixture.
In a bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, crumbled feta, and egg. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Pour this mixture evenly over the top layer in the baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Salting the eggplant draws out bitterness and excess moisture, ensuring better texture.
Browning the eggplant and sausage before baking adds depth of flavor.
traditional_techniques: Seasoning with oregano and cinnamon, characteristic of Greek savory dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Leek Soup with Crispy Smoked Sausage, Gherkin Brunoise, and Chive Oil
recipes.visual_description: A velvety, pale green leek soup fills a wide, shallow bone china bowl, leaving ample negative space. The soup's surface is smooth and pristine. Centered atop the soup is a small, artfully composed cluster of golden-brown, crispy smoked sausage crumbles. Around this, a delicate scattering of vibrant green gherkin brunoise provides a fresh, acidic contrast. A rich emerald green chive oil is meticulously drizzled in a few distinct drops across the soup's surface, creating an elegant visual pattern. A few tiny, fresh microgreens, such as chervil or pea shoots, are precisely placed for subtle height and a pop of color. The dish is presented on a premium white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures, with an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Clean leeks thoroughly. Slice white and light green parts into 1 cm rounds.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add sliced leeks. Sauté for 10-12 minutes until very soft, but not browned.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, until leeks are extremely tender.
Remove from heat. Carefully blend the soup until perfectly smooth using an immersion blender or a standing blender.
Pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan to ensure ultimate smoothness. Discard any solids.
Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm over very low heat.
Dice smoked sausage into 5 mm cubes. Render in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Finely dice gherkins into 2 mm brunoise.

For the chive oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water. Drain and squeeze dry. Blend blanched chives with neutral oil until smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear oil.
To serve, ladle the warm creamy leek soup into individual wide, shallow bowls. Do not overcrowd.
Artfully arrange a small cluster of crispy smoked sausage crumbles in the center of the soup.
Scatter gherkin brunoise delicately around the sausage.
Drizzle a few drops of chive oil onto the soup's surface. Place a few microgreens precisely for garnish.
notes: Passing the soup through a fine-mesh sieve is crucial for achieving a truly smooth, luxurious texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Pork with Potatoes and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of slow-braised pork stew is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, resting on a light wooden table. Tender, dark brown, 4-5cm chunks of braised pork shoulder are nestled amongst soft, creamy 3-4cm potato chunks and vibrant orange 2-3cm carrot pieces. The ingredients are coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown gravy, which is fluid and clings to the components. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The stew is arranged organically within the bowl, showcasing the different textures and colors. Beside the bowl, a piece of crusty baguette and a folded linen napkin complete the rustic, inviting scene. The lighting is natural and even, creating soft shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the rich gravy.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette can accompany the stew.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Cut pork shoulder into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season pork with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.

Dice onion. Peel and cut carrots into 2-3 cm thick rounds or batons. Mince garlic. Add onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce wine by half.
Stir in tomato paste. Add stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Return seared pork to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged in liquid.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 1.5 hours.
While pork braises, peel potatoes. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks.

Remove pot from oven. Add potato chunks to the stew. Stir gently. Return to oven. Continue to braise for another 45-60 minutes, or until pork and potatoes are fork-tender. Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Simmered Tomato and Basil Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous individual portion of Penne Rigate. The pasta is evenly coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce, flecked with tender pieces of slow-simmered San Marzano tomatoes and hints of green basil. A scattering of fresh, torn basil leaves provides a bright green contrast atop the pasta. A generous mound of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish, adding a creamy white texture. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware (fork and spoon). A small, rustic piece of crusty Italian bread sits beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the pasta's texture and the sauce's deep color.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer additional freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Stir in red pepper flakes.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until al dente.
Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water. Drain the pasta.
Add the cooked pasta to the tomato sauce. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Stir in half of the fresh, torn basil. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with the remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a rich, caramelized crust. A generous portion of creamy, savory mushroom sauce is spooned artfully over and around the chicken. The sauce is off-white with varying shades of earthy brown from the sliced mushrooms. The mushrooms are tender, with some retaining a slight chew. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent texture. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface beside a folded cotton napkin. Standard European flatware is neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour if using.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer 1 minute until reduced.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 2 minutes to heat through.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Apple Bundt Cake with Maple Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown Spiced Apple Bundt Cake slice sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The cake's moist crumb reveals small, tender diced apple pieces and dark specks of cinnamon and spices. A translucent, glossy maple glaze cascades gently over the cake slice, pooling slightly at the base. In the background, slightly out of focus, the full Bundt cake rests on a plain wooden cake stand on a well-used wooden dining table. A casually placed cloth napkin and warm, inviting kitchen lighting complete the relaxed, homey setting. The scene evokes comfort and celebration, highlighting the cake's natural textures and colors.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (about 600g), peeled, cored, diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 2.4-liter Bundt pan.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter with granulated sugar and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, incorporating each fully before adding the next. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with buttermilk, beginning and ending with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in diced apples gently.
Pour batter into the prepared Bundt pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 55-65 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in the pan for 15 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together powdered sugar, maple syrup, and milk until smooth. Adjust milk for desired consistency.
Drizzle glaze over the cooled cake before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragu with Pappardelle and Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragu is presented on an everyday round ceramic plate. The wide, flat pappardelle pasta forms a base, generously coated and intertwined with the rich, deep reddish-brown ragu. Tender, irregular chunks of braised beef, browned and succulent, are nestled amongst glossy, sliced cremini mushrooms. The sauce is thick, clinging to the pasta, with visible flecks of diced carrots and celery. Alongside, a modest pile of roasted Brussels sprouts, halved, show caramelized edges and a vibrant green interior. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a verdant contrast. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with simple flatware, a casually placed cloth napkin, and warm, cozy kitchen lighting creating an inviting, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Cook on low heat for 2 hours, or transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C for 2 hours. Beef should be tender.
While ragu cooks, trim Brussels sprouts and cut in half. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast Brussels sprouts in the oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and caramelized. If using oven for ragu, roast sprouts separately or after ragu finishes.
Slice cremini mushrooms. Add to the ragu during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Continue to simmer, uncovered, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Serve generous portions of ragu over cooked pappardelle. Top with roasted Brussels sprouts. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle, Roasted Mushrooms, and Brussels Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: A generous serving of wide, golden pappardelle pasta is gently tossed with rich, dark red beef ragu, featuring tender, slow-braised beef chunks and a rustic tomato sauce. The pasta spirals naturally on a clean white porcelain plate, creating a balanced, organized composition. Alongside the pasta, vibrant green, caramelized Brussels sprout halves and earthy brown, roasted mushroom slices are artfully arranged, adding texture and color contrast. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese crowns the dish, with scattered bright green fresh parsley providing a final flourish. The presentation is professional yet approachable, reflecting a hearty Italian meal. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a fork, spoon, knife, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and depth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a robust red wine.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While ragu braises, prepare vegetables. Toss sliced mushrooms and halved Brussels sprouts with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast vegetables on a baking sheet at 200°C (400°F) for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and caramelized.
Once ragu is done, remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme sprigs. Shred beef slightly with two forks if desired, or leave in chunks. Adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving some pasta water.
Add cooked pappardelle directly to the ragu. Toss to combine. Add a splash of pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Serve pasta and ragu onto individual plates. Top with roasted mushrooms and Brussels sprouts.
Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Browning the beef thoroughly is crucial for deep flavor.
Do not overcrowd the pot when searing beef; work in batches.
The ragu can be made a day ahead and reheated slowly for enhanced flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Bacon, Egg, and Tomato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Bacon, Egg, and Tomato Skillet is served on a round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The golden-brown baked egg mixture, fluffy and set, is studded with crispy, irregular chunks of bacon and bright red, slightly softened tomato wedges. Diced, roasted potatoes, browned and tender, are visible throughout the dish, interspersed with wilted dark green spinach. A light sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley garnishes the top. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, slightly distressed, suggestive of a homely family kitchen. A simple fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate, with a folded cloth napkin nearby. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a natural, uncrowded arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet to individual plates.
Accompanied by crusty bread or toast.
Often served with hot sauce or ketchup on the side for individual preference.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Chop bacon into 2 cm pieces.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Cut tomatoes into wedges.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add diced potatoes. Cook until tender and slightly browned, about 10-12 minutes. Remove potatoes from skillet.
Add bacon to the skillet. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon, reserving 15ml of bacon fat in the skillet.
Add onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato wedges and spinach. Cook until spinach wilts and tomatoes soften slightly, about 3-4 minutes.
Return cooked potatoes and bacon to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Whisk eggs with salt and pepper in a bowl.
Pour whisked eggs evenly over the skillet contents.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the eggs.
Cook on stovetop until edges of eggs set, about 5 minutes.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until eggs are fully set in the center.
Remove from oven. Let rest for a few minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: This dish is versatile. Feel free to add other vegetables like bell peppers or mushrooms for extra flavor and nutrition.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, vibrant green pea risotto rests on a clean white porcelain plate, slightly flowing and not rigid. The risotto has a fluid consistency, studded with bright green peas and flecks of fresh mint. A perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, skin-side up and golden-crisp, is placed atop the risotto, slightly off-center. The salmon flesh, a beautiful orange-pink, peeks out. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped fresh mint and a few strands of lemon zest garnish the dish, adding freshness and color. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, with a subtly blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Remove salmon from pan. Keep warm.
In a separate pot, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter over medium heat.
Add finely diced shallot. Cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add hot broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously until each addition is absorbed before adding the next.
After 15 minutes, add frozen green peas. Continue adding broth and stirring.
Cook for 5-7 more minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter, grated Parmesan, and chopped mint.
Add lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve risotto immediately. Top each portion with a seared salmon fillet.
notes: For best results, use good quality Arborio rice and fresh Parmesan.
Keep the broth hot to maintain the risotto's cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is key for a creamy texture.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming the risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-side up, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is a rich, crinkled golden-brown, glistening slightly, revealing tender meat. Beside it, a cluster of two to three irregularly shaped, golden-crisp smashed potatoes. These potatoes boast a craggy, caramelized exterior and a soft, fluffy interior. A glossy, amber-brown pan sauce is elegantly drizzled over the chicken and potatoes. Vibrant green chopped parsley and a small rosemary sprig garnish the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, emphasizing the dish's appealing textures and warm colors.
