instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5-6 cm chunks. Pat dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Slice onions thinly. Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and broth. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Return seared pork to the pot.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and braise for 2 to 2.5 hours.
Pork is ready when it is fork-tender. Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley and grated Pecorino Romano.
notes: For best flavor, braise the day before and gently reheat. The flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Gamberi all'Arancia con Polenta Cremosa, Patate Arrosto e Funghi
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain plate holds a single, refined serving. A generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, golden polenta forms the base, its surface gently rippling. Four plump, pan-seared shrimp, vibrant orange-pink with a slight char, are nestled gracefully on the polenta, their tails slightly curled. Around the base of the polenta, scattered artfully, are small, golden-brown cubes of roasted potato, their edges crisp. Thinly sliced, sautéed cremini mushrooms, dark and earthy, are interspersed among the shrimp and polenta, adding depth. A light, glistening orange-garlic pan sauce is drizzled sparingly over the shrimp and polenta, catching the light. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley and a delicate curl of orange zest. The table is a simple wooden surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware beside the plate. Natural, soft light highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer a side of crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce and polenta.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and pat dry potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Toss potato cubes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Set aside.
Zest half of the orange. Juice the entire orange. Mince 2 cloves of garlic.
In a bowl, combine shrimp with 15 ml olive oil, orange zest, half of the minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat. Set aside.

Bring 800 ml shrimp stock to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes, or until polenta is creamy and thick. Add more stock if needed for desired consistency.
Remove polenta from heat. Stir in 30 grams butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm. This technique is called 'mantecare'.

Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add 15 ml olive oil. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add remaining minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more. Season with salt and pepper. Remove mushrooms from pan. Set aside.
Increase heat in the same pan to high. Add marinated shrimp in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side, until pink and cooked through. Remove shrimp from pan.

Deglaze the pan with orange juice and a splash of shrimp stock. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced. Stir in remaining 20 grams butter. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Arrange shrimp on top of the polenta. Scatter roasted potato cubes and sautéed mushrooms around the dish. Drizzle with the orange-garlic pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a small orange segment.
notes: Adjust polenta consistency by adding more stock as needed. It should be creamy, not stiff.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Gamberi e Arancia con Crostini di Polenta e Patate al Rosmarino
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, flowing risotto is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto has a pale, warm orange hue, flecked with bright green parsley and delicate orange zest. Whole, plump, pink-orange shrimp are artfully scattered atop the risotto. To one side, a small cluster of golden-brown, crispy polenta cubes (crostini) provides textural contrast. On the opposite side, a neat mound of roasted potato cubes, golden-brown and slightly irregular, with visible flecks of dark green rosemary, adds a rustic touch. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and classic Italian flatware (a fork and a wide spoon for the risotto). Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Offer a side of crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (mopping up sauce), though risotto is typically eaten with a spoon.
Finish with an extra drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil.
instructions: Prepare Polenta Crostini: Bring 400 ml water to a boil. Add a pinch of salt. Slowly whisk in instant polenta. Cook according to package directions until thick. Spread polenta evenly onto a greased baking tray to 1 cm thickness. Let cool completely and firm up. Once firm, cut into 1.5 cm cubes.

Roast Potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Set aside.

Cook Shrimp: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add shrimp. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from pan and set aside. Deglaze pan with 1 tablespoon orange juice; reserve liquid.
Start Risotto: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Do not brown.
Add rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges. Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add 1 ladle of hot shrimp stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.

When rice is al dente (creamy but with a slight bite), remove from heat. Stir in diced cold butter, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, orange zest, and remaining orange juice. Add reserved shrimp pan liquid. Stir vigorously until creamy. This is 'mantecatura'.
Gently fold in cooked shrimp and chopped parsley. Check seasoning and adjust with salt and pepper.
Fry Polenta Crostini: Heat a small amount of olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add polenta cubes. Fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels.

Serve immediately. Ladle risotto onto warm plates. Arrange roasted potatoes and crispy polenta crostini alongside the risotto. Garnish with a fresh orange zest curl and a sprig of rosemary or parsley.
notes: Ensure shrimp stock is always hot when adding to risotto to maintain cooking temperature.
Do not overcook the shrimp; they will continue to cook slightly when added to the hot risotto.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Tonkatsu with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tonkatsu with Steamed Rice is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a light wooden table. The hero, Tonkatsu, is cut into thick 1.5 cm slices, arranged neatly but not fanned, allowing the golden-brown, crispy panko crust and tender white pork interior to be clearly visible. Beside it, a portion of fluffy, pearly white Japanese short-grain rice is mounded in a small, traditional ceramic rice bowl. A generous pile of finely shredded pale green cabbage, providing a textural contrast, sits adjacent to the Tonkatsu. A dark, glossy Tonkatsu sauce is drizzled artistically over the cutlet slices, adding rich color and shine. The overall color palette is warm golden browns, crisp whites, and fresh greens. The setting includes a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting on a ceramic chopstick rest next to the rice bowl, and a simple folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The background shows a hint of a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of miso soup.
Offer karashi (Japanese mustard) for an extra kick.
Serve with pickled ginger or tsukemono (Japanese pickles).

ingredients.name: Pork loin
ingredients.quantity: 4 pieces, 150g each, boneless, about 2 cm thick

instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot with 360ml water. Let stand 10 minutes after cooking.
Pat pork loin dry. Make shallow cuts along the edges of the pork to prevent curling. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in another, and panko in a third.
Dredge each pork loin in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, ensuring full coverage. Coat thoroughly with panko, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 170°C. Carefully lower one or two breaded pork cutlets into the hot oil. Fry for 4-5 minutes, flipping once, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove tonkatsu from oil. Drain on a wire rack set over paper towels. Let rest 2 minutes. Repeat with remaining cutlets.
Slice each tonkatsu into 1.5 cm wide strips.
Serve sliced tonkatsu immediately with steamed rice, shredded cabbage, and a drizzle of tonkatsu sauce.
notes: Ensure oil temperature is consistent for even cooking and crispness.
Do not overcrowd the pot when frying to maintain oil temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Gratin served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The base features thinly sliced 3mm potato rounds, layered and baked in a creamy, nutmeg-infused sauce. The surface has a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère cheese with caramelized edges. Two whole, pan-seared chicken thighs with crispy, deep-brown skin sit centrally atop the gratin. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork. Natural lighting highlights the contrast between the creamy sauce and the roasted chicken skin. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty French baguette to soak up the cream sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in a sharp dijon vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir
instructions: Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Whisk heavy cream, chicken stock, garlic, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Arrange half the potato slices in a greased ceramic baking dish.
Sprinkle 75g of Gruyère over the potatoes.
Layer the remaining potatoes on top.
Pour the cream mixture evenly over the potatoes.
Place the whole chicken thighs on top of the potato layers.
Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the dish.
Broil for 3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Using a mandoline ensures even potato slices for consistent cooking.
Dry the chicken skin thoroughly before searing to ensure maximum crispiness.
Check the thickest part of the chicken thigh to confirm it reaches 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage, Apple and Cheese Strata with Tomato-Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown square of Sausage, Apple and Cheese Strata occupies the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The strata's top crust is rich, speckled with caramelized cheese and visible pieces of cooked sausage chunks and small, tender apple cubes. The interior, revealed by a clean cut, shows a moist, custardy texture with soft 2 cm bread cubes, crumbled sausage chunks, and small, tender 1 cm apple cubes. The colors are warm: golden brown from the crust, creamy white from the ricotta, and savory brown from the sausage. To the side, a vibrant fresh salad of 1.5 cm diced red tomatoes and 1.5 cm green cucumber cubes, lightly dressed with a creamy white Greek yogurt dressing, adds a refreshing contrast. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes both the strata and the salad. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. A single, refined restaurant portion, with the entire plate clearly visible and appropriate negative space.

ingredients.name: Stale bread (sourdough or rustic white), cut into 2 cm cubes
Ricotta cheese (or other fresh, soft cheese)
Medium apple (e.g., Gala or Honeycrisp), cored and diced into 1 cm cubes
Medium tomatoes, diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Medium cucumber, diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish with 15g butter.
Heat remaining 15g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add sausage to the pan. Break apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in diced apple. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened. Remove from heat. Stir in 30g chopped fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Add 2 cm bread cubes to the egg mixture. Stir to coat thoroughly. Let soak for 10 minutes.
Combine soaked bread, sausage-apple mixture, and grated Gruyere cheese in the bowl. Mix well.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish. Dot spoonfuls of ricotta cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until golden brown and set in the center. A knife inserted should come out clean.
While strata bakes, prepare the salad. In a medium bowl, combine 1.5 cm diced tomatoes and 1.5 cm diced cucumber.
In a small bowl, whisk Greek yogurt, olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper. Dress the tomato-cucumber salad with this mixture.
Let strata rest for 5 minutes after baking. Cut into 4 equal portions. Serve warm with the fresh tomato-cucumber salad. Garnish with extra fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Dark Chocolate Stew with Creamy Lemon Mashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a rich, dark brown beef stew with tender 3 cm beef chunks and softened diced carrots, celery, and onion, possessing a glossy sheen. It is artfully spooned next to a generous dollop of creamy, pale yellow mashed potatoes, which display a smooth texture and a slight swirl. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes both the stew and the potatoes, adding a pop of green. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the deep browns and reds of the stew against the lighter potatoes. The setting includes a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and knife beside the plate, and a crisp cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting to highlight the food's inviting appeal.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3 cm cubes. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add 30 g butter to the pot. Sauté diced onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While stew braises, prepare mashed potatoes. Peel and cube potatoes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash potatoes with milk and remaining 20 g butter. Season with salt and pepper.
Once stew is cooked, remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Stir in finely chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth.
Stir 50 ml heavy cream into the stew. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Zest the lemon. Squeeze 15 ml lemon juice. Stir lemon zest and lemon juice into the mashed potatoes.
Chop fresh parsley. To serve, spoon creamy lemon mashed potatoes onto plates. Top with beef and dark chocolate stew. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This rich, comforting stew offers a subtle depth from dark chocolate, which balances the savory beef. The lemon in the mashed potatoes brightens the meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Mexicano
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented on a pristine white ceramic dinner plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, cooked whole, are prominently positioned atop a generous bed of vibrant, moist orange-red long-grain rice. The rice is studded with finely diced white onion, red bell pepper, and specks of green jalapeño, offering a rich tapestry of color and texture. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is sprinkled generously over the chicken and rice. A quartered lime wedge rests beside the chicken. The plate maintains moderate negative space. The setting includes a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a small ceramic bowl of vibrant salsa roja. A stack of warm corn tortillas in a woven basket completes the authentic Mexican dining experience under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of salsa roja or pico de gallo.
Accompany with refried beans or a simple green salad.
Serve with a Mexican agua fresca.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, minced garlic, minced jalapeño, and diced bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until lightly toasted.
Stir in ground cumin and dried oregano for 1 minute. Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Scrape bottom of pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Buckwheat Groat Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of Chicken and Buckwheat Groat Pilaf is served on a round, simple ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The buckwheat groats are distinct, light brown, and fluffy, interspersed with tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (approximately 3 cm). Diced, soft carrots and onions add pops of muted orange and white, integrated throughout the pilaf. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh dill garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The pilaf is arranged naturally, forming a modest mound, with some components touching the plate's edge. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a plain metal fork. A small, white bowl containing a few sliced pickled cucumbers sits casually next to the plate. A loosely folded, simple cloth napkin is placed nearby. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere in a relaxed family dining area. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with pickled vegetables such as cucumbers or cabbage.
Often accompanied by a dollop of sour cream or kefir.
instructions: Rinse buckwheat groats thoroughly under cold water. Drain well.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and dice the onion into small cubes. Peel and dice carrots into small cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced carrots. Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add rinsed buckwheat groats. Stir to combine.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until buckwheat is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let pilaf rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Stir in chopped fresh dill before serving.
notes: Adjust liquid amount if buckwheat groats absorb more or less liquid than expected. The pilaf should be moist but not soupy.

recipes.recipe_name: Maggi-Glazed Pork Chops with Roasted Carrots and Parsnips
recipes.visual_description: A single seared, bone-in pork chop, golden-brown with a visible crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork chop is presented whole. Alongside, a vibrant medley of roasted carrots and parsnips, cut into uniform batons and wedges, display caramelized edges and a tender texture. A rich, glossy Maggi glaze pools artfully beside the chop and lightly coats the vegetables. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered sparingly for a touch of green. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal of the main components. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard flatware subtly placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating a professional and inviting image.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel carrots and parsnips. Cut into 5 cm long batons or wedges.
Toss vegetables with 30 ml olive oil, 3 thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the oven with the roasted vegetables.
Cook pork chops in the oven for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, or desired doneness. Remove from oven and rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
While pork rests, prepare the glaze. In the same skillet (or a small saucepan), combine Maggi Liquid Seasoning, honey, minced garlic, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Whisk in cold butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Strain glaze if desired for a smoother consistency.
Serve pork chops with roasted carrots and parsnips. Drizzle generously with Maggi glaze. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: The internal temperature for pork can be cooked to 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, followed by a 3-minute rest, which will bring it to a safe consumption temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Roasted Apple & Potato, Herb Pasta, and Rustic Croutons
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, capturing a modern bistro aesthetic. A golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, unsliced and whole, anchors the composition. Flanking the chicken are earthy roasted potato wedges and slightly caramelized apple wedges, showcasing a soft, tender texture with a hint of crispness. A small, neat mound of herb-tossed short pasta, glistening with a light sauce, sits adjacent. Scattered across the dish are small, golden-brown rustic bread croutons, adding a textural contrast. Fresh green parsley and rosemary sprigs provide vibrant color and a fresh aromatic garnish. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, European flatware, and a cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting to highlight the food's inviting textures and colors.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock or dry white wine

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and quarter the new potatoes. Core and cut apples into 2 cm wedges.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes and apple wedges with 30 ml olive oil, half the chopped rosemary, half the chopped thyme, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes and apples on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, presentation side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown. Flip and sear for another 5 minutes.
Transfer skillet to the oven with the roasted vegetables. Cook chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 60 ml pasta water.
Cut rustic bread into 1.5 cm cubes. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15g butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add bread cubes and cook, stirring, until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm. Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat.
Add remaining 15g butter and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze with chicken stock or white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce slightly.
Add drained pasta to the skillet sauce. Toss to coat, adding reserved pasta water if needed for consistency. Stir in remaining rosemary, thyme, and half the chopped parsley.

To serve, place a portion of pasta on each plate. Arrange a chicken thigh, roasted potatoes, and apple wedges alongside the pasta. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with rustic croutons and fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The creamy risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its fluid, natural consistency. The Arborio rice is pearlescent white, generously coated in a rich, pale yellow sauce, reflecting the butter and Parmesan. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, seared to perfection, are nestled within the risotto. Vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, slightly charred at the edges, are scattered across the top, adding a pop of color and textural contrast. Sautéed cremini mushrooms are visible throughout, contributing earthy tones. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley and delicate shavings of aged Parmesan cheese. A clean white linen napkin and a traditional fork and spoon rest beside the bowl on a simple wooden table, under soft, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping.
Present in a communal bowl for sharing, with individual serving plates.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.

Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm thick medallions. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Once cool enough, cut into 2-3 cm chunks.
Melt 30 g butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and celery. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and their liquid has evaporated.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice grains (Tostatura).
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed (Sfumatura).
Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in the cooked chicken chunks and roasted broccoli florets. Cook for 2 minutes to heat through.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese (Mantecatura). Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and additional shaved Parmesan.
notes: The key to good risotto is constant stirring and gradual addition of hot stock.
Ensure the chicken stock is hot when added to avoid cooling down the rice and interrupting the cooking process.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Apple-Pistachio Chutney
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared beef medallion, golden-brown with a savory crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, presented as a thick, whole piece (not sliced), shows a hint of its juicy, medium-rare interior. Adjacent to the beef is a vibrant mound of chunky apple-pistachio chutney, its diced apples and chopped pistachios visible, offering contrasting textures and a warm, golden-brown hue. A glistening, rich pan sauce is artfully drizzled around the beef, pooling slightly at the base. Fresh green thyme sprigs and a scattering of additional chopped pistachios provide a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred restaurant background.
instructions: Dice apples. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Roughly chop pistachios.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced apples, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, and water.
Simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and liquid reduces.
Stir in half of the chopped pistachios. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Add butter and fresh thyme to the skillet during the last minute of cooking. Baste beef with butter.
Remove beef from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5-10 minutes.
Deglaze the skillet with beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits.
Simmer broth until slightly reduced, about 2-3 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Place a beef medallion on each plate.
Spoon a generous portion of apple-pistachio chutney next to the beef.
Drizzle pan sauce over and around the beef.
Garnish with remaining chopped pistachios and fresh thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Resting the beef after searing is crucial for juiciness and even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain pasta bowl sits on a light oak bistro table. A mound of broad pappardelle ribbons is thoroughly coated in a deep red, thick tomato sauce. Large, intact chunks of slow-braised beef are distributed throughout the pasta, showing a moist, tender texture. The sauce is glossy and emulsified, featuring visible flecks of minced garlic and finely diced vegetables. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese is concentrated in the center. Three vibrant green whole basil leaves provide a fresh garnish. A heavy stainless steel fork and a white cotton napkin rest to the right. Natural side-lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the rich texture of the braised meat and the silky pasta surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to mop up remaining sauce.
Pair with a glass of Chianti or Sangiovese wine.
Present in a shallow bowl to maintain sauce temperature.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to release brown bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and browned beef.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 2.5 hours until beef is tender.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with ragu and reserved water until glossy.
Plate immediately. Top with cheese and basil.
notes: Do not shred the beef; maintain distinct chunks for texture.
Use high-quality canned tomatoes for authentic sweetness.
Ensure the pasta water is added to achieve a restaurant-quality silkiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rosemary Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a rustic white ceramic plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is the focal point. Around it are scattered golden-brown potato wedges, some with slightly charred edges, alongside soft, caramelized chunks of roasted onion and tender, smashed garlic cloves. Fresh rosemary sprigs and a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley add color and aroma. A roasted lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The overall impression is warm and hearty. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic European flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, warm light illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Roughly chop the onion. Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
Slice half of the lemon into thin rounds. Juice the other half.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken, potato wedges, chopped onion, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and lemon slices. Drizzle with olive oil. Toss everything to coat evenly.
Roast for 30 minutes. Turn chicken and potatoes.
Pour white wine and chicken broth into the pan. Stir gently.
Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden brown. Baste occasionally with pan juices.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for safety.
For extra crispness, increase oven temperature to 220°C (425°F) for the last 10 minutes, monitoring closely.
traditional_techniques: Seasoning with fresh herbs and lemon

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto with Arugula
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl holds a single portion of creamy, vibrant orange-red risotto. The risotto is fluid and free-flowing, showing the individual, plump Arborio rice grains infused with tomato. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, irregular 3 cm chunks of seared chicken thigh. A generous handful of fresh, dark green arugula leaves is artfully arranged on top, providing a crisp contrast. Specks of grated Parmesan cheese and torn fresh basil leaves are sprinkled over the dish, adding hints of white and bright green. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table. Beside the bowl, a silver fork and a deep spoon are placed on a folded light grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of crisp Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.

Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. The risotto should be fluid.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Fold in the cooked chicken chunks.
Serve immediately in wide, shallow bowls. Top each serving with fresh arugula and torn basil leaves.
notes: Achieving a truly creamy risotto requires constant stirring and gradual addition of hot stock.
Do not rinse Arborio rice.
traditional_techniques: Risotto method (toasting rice, deglazing with wine, gradual stock addition, mantecatura with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato, Cauliflower, and Carrot Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant, creamy Roasted Tomato, Cauliflower, and Carrot Soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The soup boasts a rich, orange-red hue, indicating its savory depth. A gentle swirl of crème fraîche or a light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley sits atop the smooth surface. Small, tender roasted carrot chunks are visible within, providing a subtle textural contrast. The bowl rests on a well-worn wooden dining table, showcasing its natural grain. A simple, silver soup spoon lies to the right of the bowl, with a casually folded linen napkin nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, focusing entirely on the hearty, elegantly plated soup.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley or crème fraîche (for garnish)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve tomatoes. Cut cauliflower into florets. Cut carrots into 2 cm chunks.
In a large bowl, toss halved tomatoes, cauliflower florets, and carrot chunks with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, until vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Roughly chop the onion. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Smash garlic cloves. Add to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the roasted vegetables to the pot with the sautéed onion and garlic.
Pour in 1 litre of vegetable stock. Bring the soup to a simmer.
Reduce heat and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove the pot from heat. Use an immersion blender to purée the soup until smooth.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with a swirl of crème fraîche or finely chopped fresh parsley, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Tofu and Cabbage Stir-fry is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. Golden-brown, seared 2 cm tofu cubes are nestled amongst vibrant green shredded cabbage. The dish glistens with a glossy, savory sauce that lightly coats all ingredients. A sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green spring onions garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with components slightly overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed white rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks, reflecting a homely East Asian meal setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
instructions: Press tofu block for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut pressed tofu into 2 cm cubes.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and water or vegetable broth. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes to the hot pan. Sear until golden brown and crispy on all sides. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu from pan and set aside.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the same pan. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage to the pan. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until cabbage is tender-crisp.
Return seared tofu to the pan with the cabbage.
Whisk the sauce mixture again, then pour it over the tofu and cabbage. Stir continuously until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions before serving.
notes: Pressing the tofu is crucial for achieving a crispy texture when searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Sweet Potato Puree and Crispy Brussels Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Miso-Glazed Salmon is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The salmon fillet, a vibrant orange-pink, is prominently placed, its top glistening with a rich, dark miso glaze. Its skin is golden and crispy. Beside the salmon, a smooth, creamy mound of pale orange sweet potato puree provides a soft textural contrast. Halved Brussels sprouts, deeply roasted and caramelized with crisp edges, are arranged artfully around the salmon and puree, their dark green contrasting with the brighter elements. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and finely chopped fresh green chives, adding visual interest and freshness. A small white ceramic bowl for rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rest beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a softly blurred, restaurant-style background. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space, showcasing the quality ingredients and refined preparation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed white rice.
Offer a side of pickled ginger (gari) to cleanse the palate.
Accompany with a simple side salad dressed with a light soy-sesame vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Salmon fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Prepare the miso glaze. In a small saucepan, combine miso paste, mirin, sake, sugar, soy sauce, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Whisk well.
Heat the glaze over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until sugar dissolves and mixture thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool.

Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Place salmon in a shallow dish. Spoon about half of the cooled miso glaze over the salmon. Ensure all sides are coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash and trim Brussels sprouts. Halve larger sprouts. Toss with 15 ml neutral oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Roast Brussels sprouts for 20-25 minutes. They should be tender-crisp and lightly caramelized. Toss halfway through cooking.
While sprouts roast, peel sweet potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a medium saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring sweet potatoes to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mash sweet potatoes thoroughly. Add 15 ml neutral oil, sesame oil, salt, and pepper to taste. Mix until smooth and creamy. Keep warm.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of neutral oil.
Remove salmon from marinade. Reserve remaining glaze. Place salmon fillets, skin-side down if applicable, in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). The salmon should be cooked through but still moist.
Remove salmon from oven. Brush with some of the reserved miso glaze.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of sweet potato puree onto each plate. Place a seared salmon fillet beside the puree. Arrange roasted Brussels sprouts around the salmon. Drizzle with additional reserved miso glaze. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, marinate the salmon for at least 30 minutes. Do not marinate for more than 2 hours as the miso can cure the fish too much.
Adjust the amount of sugar in the glaze to your preference; some miso pastes are saltier or sweeter than others.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Pork Loin with Herbed Breadcrumbs, Roasted Carrots, and Dijon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, featuring a refined individual portion. Two thick medallions of golden-brown, pan-seared stuffed pork loin are the centerpiece, each about 2-3 cm thick, showcasing the spiraled breadcrumb and herb filling. The pork has a slight crispness from searing and roasting. Beside the pork, a neat pile of vibrant orange roasted carrot batons, slightly caramelized at the edges, adds contrasting color and texture. A rich, creamy Dijon mustard pan sauce is elegantly spooned over the pork and lightly around the carrots. A delicate sprig of fresh thyme or parsley rests atop the pork, providing a touch of fresh green. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting quality ingredients and precise cooking. The scene features a simple wooden table, natural, even lighting, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled and cut into batons

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly pork loin: Slice lengthwise, not all the way through, then open flat. Pound lightly to even thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare stuffing: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté half of the diced onion and half of the minced garlic until soft. Remove from heat.
Combine sautéed onion/garlic with breadcrumbs, half of the chopped parsley, chopped thyme, 5g Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spread stuffing evenly over the butterflied pork loin. Roll up tightly. Secure with kitchen twine.
Sear pork: Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork roll on all sides until golden brown.
Roast pork and carrots: Add carrot batons to the pan around the pork. Season carrots with salt and pepper. Transfer pan to preheated oven.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until pork internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove pork from pan. Let rest 10 minutes, covered loosely. Carrots should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Make sauce: Return pan to stovetop over medium heat. Add remaining diced onion and garlic. Sauté until soft.
Add chicken stock and remaining 25g Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce sauce by half, stirring occasionally. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in remaining chopped parsley.
Slice pork: Remove twine. Slice pork loin into thick medallions (about 2-3 cm thick).
Plate: Arrange pork medallions and roasted carrots on plates. Spoon Dijon sauce over and around the pork. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: German Pork and Carrot Soup with Crispy Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic white ceramic bowl holds a single serving of hearty German Pork and Carrot Soup. The rich, golden-brown broth is filled with tender, 2cm diced pork cubes and vibrant 1cm diced carrots and softened onion pieces. The soup is generously garnished with a sprinkle of golden-brown, crispy toasted breadcrumbs and a scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley on top. The composition is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space around the bowl. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and a sturdy, traditional German-style spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's textures and colors, with a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of hearty rye bread.
Traditionally accompanied by a crisp German lager.
instructions: Dice pork shoulder into 2cm cubes. Season pork with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion and 1cm diced carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 1 minute.
Return pork to the pot. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until pork is very tender.
While soup simmers, melt butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and toast, stirring constantly, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside.
Taste soup and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with toasted breadcrumbs and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Escalopes with Herbed Parmesan Crumb
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown, crispy pan-fried pork escalope, presented whole, occupies the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The escalope is oval, thin, and displays a textured, golden-brown crumb. It rests gracefully on a small, vibrant bed of fresh arugula leaves, lightly dressed. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the escalope, ready to be squeezed. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley garnishes the top of the pork. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting. The plate is positioned on a rustic light wood table, alongside a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the crisp texture of the pork and the freshness of the greens.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad, such as arugula with a lemon vinaigrette.
Traditionally accompanied by roasted potatoes or a side of seasonal vegetables.
Often served with extra lemon wedges for a fresh squeeze over the hot escalope.

ingredients.name: Olive oil (or vegetable oil for frying)

instructions: Slice pork loin into 4 equal portions. Place each portion between two sheets of cling film.
Pound each pork portion with a mallet until approximately 5 mm thick. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Prepare a breading station. Place flour in a shallow dish. In a second shallow dish, beat eggs. In a third shallow dish, combine Panko breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, minced garlic, finely minced shallot, and chopped parsley. Mix well.
Dredge each pork escalope in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Finally, coat thoroughly with the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Ensure oil is shimmering.
Carefully place 2 escalopes in the hot pan. Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 71°C (160°F).
Transfer cooked escalopes to a wire rack to drain excess oil. Keep warm. Repeat with remaining escalopes.
Slice lemons into wedges. Arrange each escalope on a plate with a side of fresh arugula leaves. Garnish with lemon wedges.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Pork Meatball & Orzo Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Italian Pork Meatball & Orzo Soup in a deep, white porcelain bowl. The clear, warm orange-red tomato-infused broth contains small, round, browned pork meatballs (approx. 3cm diameter) and delicate orzo pasta. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are visible. Garnish with vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley leaves, a light drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil, and a sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan. A small pile of golden-brown, crispy breadcrumbs rests on the bowl's rim. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, with a silver spoon and folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the steam, creating a professional bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork, 60 g breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan cheese, half of the chopped parsley, dried oregano, 2 minced garlic cloves, half of the finely diced onion, 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined.
Form the mixture into small, 3 cm diameter meatballs.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add meatballs. Brown meatballs on all sides. Remove meatballs and set aside.
Add remaining 10 ml olive oil to the pot. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and remaining diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the soup to a simmer.
Return browned meatballs to the pot. Add orzo pasta. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until orzo is al dente and meatballs are cooked through (internal temperature 71°C).
While soup cooks, toast the extra 30 g breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and crispy. Set aside for garnish.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley, a drizzle of olive oil, a sprinkle of Parmesan, and toasted crispy breadcrumbs.
notes: Ensure meatballs are cooked to a safe internal temperature.
Adjust herb quantities to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Pasta and Apple-Potato Medley
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and resting whole. Adjacent to it, a generous portion of penne pasta, lightly coated in a vibrant lemon-herb sauce, is artfully piled. Around the base of the chicken and pasta, a colorful medley of 1.5 cm diced potatoes and apples is scattered, with some potato cubes exhibiting a light golden crust and apple pieces showing subtle caramelization. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the entire dish, and a bright yellow lemon wedge is positioned for a pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro style.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove and rest chicken.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, peel potatoes. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Core apples and dice into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic and shallot. Chop parsley and thyme.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a separate large skillet over medium heat. Add diced potatoes. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned.
Add diced apples to the potato skillet. Cook 3-5 minutes, until apples soften slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add minced shallot and garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze with chicken broth. Add lemon juice (from half a lemon) and chopped thyme. Simmer 2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed to create a light sauce. Toss to coat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
To serve, plate pasta. Top with rested chicken breast. Arrange apple-potato medley around the chicken and pasta. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken rests after cooking to retain juices.
Adjust lemon juice to your preference for acidity.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chickpea and Eggplant Stew
recipes.visual_description: The Moroccan Chickpea and Eggplant Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with an earthy, matte finish. The stew itself is a rich, reddish-brown, teeming with tender 2 cm cubes of eggplant, whole chickpeas, and vibrant specks of chopped dried apricots. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro and parsley crowns the dish, contrasting beautifully with the stew's deep colors. The sauce has a moderate consistency, clinging to the ingredients. A single lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white linen napkin, and a side serving of fluffy couscous in a smaller matching bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's inviting textures and steam.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy couscous
Offer with warm, crusty flatbread for dipping
Provide a side of harissa paste for those who prefer more heat
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Place in a colander. Sprinkle with 5g salt. Let sit 30 minutes. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, ginger, and cinnamon. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add dried eggplant cubes. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned and softened.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock, and drained chickpeas. Add chopped dried apricots. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until eggplant is very tender and flavors have melded. Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat. Stir in chopped fresh cilantro, fresh parsley, and lemon juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: Salting the eggplant draws out moisture and bitterness, resulting in a better texture.
Adjust spice levels to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Sausage, Ricotta, and Pecorino
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked rigatoni is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing its comforting warmth. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato and crumbled sausage sauce. Creamy white pockets of ricotta cheese are visible throughout the pasta, offering a soft contrast to the robust sauce. The top layer of Pecorino Romano cheese is melted and golden-brown, with some slightly crisped edges. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are torn and scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is arranged naturally, with pasta intertwining, not overly structured. It rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded linen napkin and traditional Italian flatware. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and optional red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Italian pork sausage, crumbled. Cook until browned, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
Pour in crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer sauce for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in half of the fresh basil.
Cook rigatoni pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente, about 2 minutes less than package directions. Drain well.
Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Stir to coat evenly.
Gently fold in ricotta cheese, leaving some visible pockets.
Transfer the pasta mixture to a 3-liter baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan.
Sprinkle evenly with grated Pecorino Romano cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and the cheese is golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente before baking to prevent it from becoming mushy in the oven.
Using high-quality San Marzano tomatoes will significantly enhance the sauce flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Tagliatelle al Ricotta e Piselli
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents freshly cooked tagliatelle, coiled neatly into a modest mound at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy, pale ivory sauce, created from fresh ricotta and Pecorino Romano, with a slight sheen from olive oil. Vibrant green pea shoots are gently folded throughout the pasta, adding bursts of color and tender texture. Finely grated Pecorino Romano is lightly sprinkled over the top, along with a few fresh, upright pea shoots for garnish. A delicate drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil finishes the presentation. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic Italian flatware, against a subtly blurred modern bistro background with soft, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up any remaining sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Boil 4 litres of salted water in a large pot. Cook 400g tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente.
Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water before draining the tagliatelle.
While pasta cooks, heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add 2 finely minced garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add 100g pea shoots to the pan. Sauté 1-2 minutes until just wilted. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine 250g fresh ricotta, 70g grated Pecorino Romano, zest of 1 lemon, and juice of half a lemon. Season with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Add the drained tagliatelle to the bowl with the ricotta mixture. Add 125ml of the reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously, adding more pasta water gradually until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms, coating the pasta.
Fold in the wilted pea shoots.
Serve immediately. Drizzle each portion with remaining 30ml extra virgin olive oil. Garnish with remaining grated Pecorino and fresh pea shoots.
notes: Use high-quality fresh ricotta for the best creamy texture.
Adjust the amount of Pecorino Romano to your taste for saltiness and pungency.
traditional_techniques: Emulsification of pasta sauce with starchy pasta water

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Dijon Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of golden-seared chicken medallions, nestled within a rich, creamy Dijon mushroom sauce. The chicken, cut into thick, irregular chunks, shows a beautiful caramelized crust. The sauce, a warm ivory hue, coats the chicken and tender, quartered cremini mushrooms. Alongside, several crisp-skinned, fluffy-centered potato wedges are neatly arranged. A sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of green. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, resting on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a standard set of flatware complete the casual bistro setting under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing can accompany the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut small potatoes in half or larger ones into wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes until golden and tender.
Cut chicken breasts into thick medallions, about 2-3cm thick. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken medallions. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Dice the shallot finely and add to the skillet. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.

Halve or quarter cremini mushrooms depending on size. Add mushrooms to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Mince garlic and add to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Whisk in Dijon mustard. Stir in heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Return seared chicken medallions to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes to heat through. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Stir most of the parsley into the sauce. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve chicken and mushroom sauce immediately with roasted potatoes alongside. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer to reduce or adding a splash more stock/cream if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Sesame Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks are centrally arranged amidst a vibrant medley of crisp-tender vegetables. Julienne-cut carrots, bright green bean pieces, and thin strips of red and yellow bell peppers are artfully tossed with yellow corn kernels, all glistening with a savory, glossy sauce. Freshly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds add a final touch of color and texture. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A small, white rice bowl with steamed white rice sits beside the main plate, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks, ready for a modern bistro dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice on the side.
Offer chopsticks for dining.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, trimmed, cut into 3 cm pieces

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, julienned or cut into thin batons

ingredients.name: Chili flakes (gochugaru or red pepper flakes)

instructions: Combine soy sauce, 15 ml toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, brown sugar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and chili flakes in a bowl. Whisk well.
In a separate small bowl, dissolve cornstarch in 60 ml water or chicken stock. Add this slurry to the sauce mixture. Stir to combine.
Heat 15 ml neutral cooking oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook until browned and cooked through, approximately 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml neutral cooking oil to the wok. Add julienned carrots and green beans. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add bell pepper strips and corn kernels to the wok. Continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Vegetables should remain vibrant and crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok with the vegetables.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the chicken and vegetables. Stir constantly until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in the remaining 15 ml toasted sesame oil.
Serve immediately, garnished with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork with Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork with Cabbage is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thin slices of seared pork belly, 3mm thick and 5cm long, are mixed with vibrant green, tender-crisp cabbage wedges and translucent onion slices. The dish glistens with a rich, reddish-brown sauce, flecked with bright red dried chili segments and dark fermented black beans. A sprinkle of thinly sliced vibrant green spring onions adds a fresh counterpoint. The composition is balanced and moderately filled, allowing for appropriate negative space. Beside the plate, a small, pristine white rice bowl holds fluffy jasmine rice. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a ceramic holder. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, natural even lighting, and a subtle, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family style, with individual bowls of steamed jasmine rice for each diner.
Offer chopsticks as the primary utensil.
instructions: Place pork belly in a pot. Cover with water. Add half of the ginger piece and 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until pork is tender, about 25-30 minutes. Drain pork. Let cool completely.
Slice cooled pork belly into 3 mm thick, 5 cm long pieces.
Core green cabbage. Cut into 4 cm wedges. Slice onion into 1 cm wide wedges. Mince remaining ginger and garlic. Cut dried chilies into 2 cm segments.
Heat a wok over high heat. Add 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Add sliced pork belly. Stir-fry until edges curl and fat renders, about 5-7 minutes. Remove pork from wok. Leave rendered fat in wok.

Add doubanjiang, fermented black beans, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns to the wok with rendered fat. Stir-fry until fragrant and oil turns red, about 1 minute. Add minced garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return pork to the wok. Add cabbage wedges and onion wedges. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cabbage is tender-crisp.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and sugar. Stir-fry briefly to combine all ingredients.
Transfer the dish to a serving platter. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions. Serve immediately with jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Braised Squash and Green Lentils
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is presented on a round white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of fluffy couscous forms the base. The Moroccan braised squash and green lentils are generously spooned over the couscous, allowing some of the rich, reddish-brown sauce to pool around the base. The butternut squash is cut into distinct 3-4 cm cubes, showcasing its golden-orange color and tender texture. The green lentils are visible, providing an earthy texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh cilantro and parsley, adding vibrant green color. The plate sits on a simple, rustic wooden table surface. A folded, deep jewel-toned cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. A small, decorative ceramic bowl containing a side of bright orange harissa or yellow preserved lemon wedges sits next to the main plate, enhancing cultural authenticity. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional couscous or crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a side of harissa for heat or preserved lemons for tang.
instructions: Peel, deseed, and cut butternut squash into 3-4 cm cubes.
Dice the onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, sweet paprika, and cinnamon stick. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add green lentils, squash cubes, vegetable broth, and canned diced tomatoes. Stir well.
Soak saffron threads in 30ml warm water for 5 minutes. Add saffron and water to the pot.
Add halved dried apricots. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lentils are tender and squash is soft. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in most of the chopped fresh cilantro and parsley. Reserve some for garnish.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in lemon juice.
Prepare couscous according to package directions.
Serve the Moroccan braised squash and green lentils hot, spooned over the prepared couscous. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro and parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Chicken with Cashews and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A single portion features glistening, 2cm diced chicken, stir-fried to a light golden hue, intermingled with vibrant green broccoli florets and golden-brown roasted cashews. Ingredients are evenly coated in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown sauce, hinting at savory, sweet, and spicy notes. Small, whole dried red chilies and dark Sichuan peppercorns add visual depth. Diced onions provide subtle texture. The arrangement is organic and flowing, with ingredients well-distributed. Moderate negative space surrounds the central mound. Beside the plate, a cotton napkin and dark wooden chopsticks rest. A small white bowl of fluffy jasmine rice accompanies the main dish. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's texture and sheen, against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer chopsticks for eating.
Serve in individual bowls.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. In a bowl, toss chicken with 10ml soy sauce, 15ml Shaoxing wine, 5g cornstarch, and a pinch of salt and white pepper. Marinate 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining 35ml soy sauce, 15ml Shaoxing wine, Chinkiang vinegar, sugar, remaining 10g cornstarch, and 60ml water or stock. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Cook 1-2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the wok. Stir-fry 2 minutes until fragrant and onion softens slightly.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add blanched broccoli and roasted cashews. Give the prepared sauce a quick whisk, then pour into the wok.
Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients. Stir in sesame oil.
Transfer to a serving dish. Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: Adjust dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns to taste for desired spice level.
Ensure cashews are roasted for best flavor and texture; if raw, toast lightly in a dry pan before adding.

recipes.recipe_name: Bean Sprout and Herb Salad with Pan-Seared Salmon
recipes.special_requests: no carrot, no pork, no fruits
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, colorful salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base features a generous mound of crisp mixed greens, intermingled with delicate white bean sprouts, bright green sliced spring onions, and vibrant julienned cucumber and red bell pepper. Fresh green mint and cilantro leaves are visible throughout, adding texture and aroma. Pan-seared salmon chunks, with their slightly caramelized, golden-brown crust and rosy interior, are artfully placed on top of the salad. A light, clear dressing glistens on the ingredients, coating them evenly. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of golden crushed peanuts and tiny toasted sesame seeds, offering textural contrast. The overall composition is fresh, abundant, and naturally arranged, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a fork, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra dressing on the side for individual preference.
Offer additional fresh chili slices or Sriracha for those desiring more heat.
Traditionally enjoyed as a refreshing appetizer or light meal.
instructions: Prepare the dressing. Combine lime juice, fish sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, minced garlic, and sliced chili (if using) in a small bowl. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove salmon from pan. Let rest for a few minutes. Break into large flakes or chunks.
In a large mixing bowl, combine bean sprouts, mixed salad greens, sliced spring onions, julienned cucumber, julienned red bell pepper, chopped mint, and chopped cilantro.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Divide salad among four plates.
Top each salad with flaked salmon pieces.
Garnish with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili quantity in the dressing to your preferred spice level.
Ensure salmon is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
For a vegetarian option, omit salmon and add pan-fried tofu or edamame.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Pork Belly with Bean Sprout Salad
