Remove the pork from the oven and transfer it to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender pork.
While the pork rests, return the skillet to medium heat on the stovetop. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of maple syrup and the Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the sauce slightly thickens.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the unsalted butter until melted and incorporated, creating a glossy pan sauce.

Slice the rested pork tenderloins into 1-inch thick medallions. Serve immediately with the roasted butternut squash and drizzle generously with the pan sauce. Garnish with a few fresh sage leaves if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Garlic Beef Noodle Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, hearty one-pan skillet dish filled with tender wide egg noodles and savory ground beef in a rich, slightly thickened brown sauce. The dish is flecked with bits of sautéed onion, minced garlic, and dried oregano, with a vibrant green garnish of fresh parsley on top. Steam gently rises from the comforting meal, presented in a cast-iron skillet on a rustic wooden surface, inviting and warm.

instructions.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Drain any excess fat.
Add chopped onion to the skillet with the beef and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, dried oregano, and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Add the egg noodles to the skillet, stirring to ensure they are submerged in the liquid. Bring back to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until noodles are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove from heat. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let stand for 2-3 minutes before serving to allow the sauce to thicken slightly. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Garlic Beef & Oregano Noodles Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic skillet dish featuring tender ground beef and al dente spaghetti noodles, richly coated in a vibrant, savory tomato-based sauce. The dish is infused with aromatic minced garlic and earthy dried oregano, presenting a warm and inviting appearance, perfect for a comforting casual meal. It's served directly from a large, well-seasoned skillet, highlighting its homemade charm.

instructions.instruction: Prepare ingredients: Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and break the spaghetti into 2-3 inch pieces. Have all other ingredients measured and ready.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until thoroughly browned. Drain any excess fat from the skillet. Remove the cooked beef and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped onion to the same skillet and cook until softened and translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and dried oregano, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Return the cooked beef to the skillet. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Stir everything together and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

Add the broken spaghetti to the skillet, stirring well to ensure the noodles are submerged in the liquid. Cover the skillet, reduce the heat to low, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.

Season the dish with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well to combine. Let the skillet rest off the heat for a few minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Garlic Beef Noodle Bites
recipes.visual_description: A close-up shot of a small, elegant serving bowl filled with glistening, thinly sliced beef strips intertwined with tender, golden-brown thin egg noodles. The dish is coated in a rich, savory, slightly glossy sauce, flecked with finely minced garlic and vibrant green specks of dried oregano and fresh chopped green onions. The beef has a beautiful caramelized edge, and the noodles are perfectly coated, showing a slight sheen. The overall impression is warm, inviting, and appetizing, with steam subtly rising from the dish. The background is softly blurred, enhancing focus on the dish.

ingredients.name: Red pepper flakes
ingredients.notes: optional, for a hint of heat

instructions.instruction: Prepare Beef: Slice the beef against the grain into thin strips. In a medium bowl, combine the beef with 1 tablespoon of low-sodium soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, 2 minced garlic cloves, 0.5 teaspoon of dried oregano, 0.5 teaspoon of salt, and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper. Mix well to ensure the beef is evenly coated. Let it marinate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 30 minutes.

Cook Noodles: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the thin egg noodles (or vermicelli) and cook according to package directions until al dente, typically 5-7 minutes. Drain the noodles well and rinse briefly with cold water to prevent them from sticking together. Set aside.

Stir-fry Beef: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering. Add the marinated beef in a single layer (cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding, which can steam the beef instead of browning it). Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked beef from the skillet and set aside.

Sauté Aromatics: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the skillet. Add the remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon of dried oregano (and red pepper flakes, if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

Create Sauce & Combine Noodles: Pour in the 0.5 cup of beef broth and the remaining 1 tablespoon of low-sodium soy sauce. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Add the cooked noodles to the skillet and toss well to coat them evenly in the sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing the noodles to absorb some of the liquid and flavors.

Final Combination: Return the cooked beef to the skillet with the noodles. Toss everything together for 1 minute until heated through and well combined, ensuring the beef is thoroughly incorporated with the noodles and sauce.
Serve: Transfer the Savory Garlic Beef Noodle Bites to serving bowls. Garnish generously with freshly chopped green onions before serving immediately as a savory starter for 4 people.

recipes.recipe_name: Tangy Gherkin & Dijon Chicken Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic yet elegant skillet dish featuring four golden-brown seared chicken breasts generously coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce. The sauce is visibly flecked with finely chopped bright green gherkins and fresh green parsley, offering a delightful contrast in color and texture. The dish is presented in a dark, cast-iron skillet, hinting at its comforting, home-cooked nature. A subtle wisp of steam gently rises from the warm sauce, and the chicken appears tender and moist, ready to be enjoyed.

ingredients.name: Chicken Breasts
ingredients.unit: pieces (approx. 6-8 oz each per piece, boneless, skinless)

instructions.instruction: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season both sides of the chicken with 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium-high heat. Once hot, sear the chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown. The chicken will not be cooked through at this point. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside on a plate.

Reduce heat to medium. Add unsalted butter to the same skillet. Add the finely diced yellow onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.

If using flour for thickening, sprinkle the tablespoon of all-purpose flour over the onions and garlic, and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon to deglaze. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Whisk in the Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Stir in the finely chopped gherkins. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 2-3 minutes to slightly thicken. Season the sauce with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper, or to taste.

Return the seared chicken breasts to the skillet, nestling them into the creamy gherkin sauce. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the skillet, and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
Remove the skillet from the heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Serve immediately with your preferred side dish, such as rice, mashed potatoes, or pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Träume mit Hähnchen-Essenz-Gelée
recipes.visual_description: A delicate, airy lemon-rosemary mousse, elegantly piped into a serving glass or set on a plate, adorned with glistening cubes of transparent, pale golden chicken essence gelée. Crispy, golden-brown rosemary sugar tuile shards are artfully placed, providing textural contrast. Thin, translucent strips of candied lemon peel curl gracefully, catching the light. The overall presentation is refined, minimalist, and visually light, with subtle hints of green from the rosemary.

ingredients.name: Lemons
ingredients.notes: For 100ml juice and 2 tsp zest for mousse, plus 1 peel for garnish

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Sweet Chicken Essence Gelée: Place diced chicken breast, cold water, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a very gentle simmer over low heat. Cook for 30-40 minutes, skimming any foam that rises to the surface, ensuring the liquid remains clear.

Strain the chicken stock very carefully through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth into a clean bowl. Discard solids. Bloom the gelatin sheet in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.

Gently heat 50ml of the strained chicken stock, remove from heat, squeeze excess water from gelatin, and dissolve it in the warm stock. Stir in the 20g granulated sugar until fully dissolved. Combine the sweetened gelatin mixture with the remaining clear chicken stock. Pour into a shallow, flat dish (e.g., a small baking dish or plate) to a depth of about 0.5 cm.
Chill the chicken gelée in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until fully set. Once set, cut the gelée into small, uniform cubes (approximately 0.5 cm).

Prepare the Candied Lemon Peel Garnish: Place the lemon peel strips in a small saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain and repeat this process two more times (total 3 blanchings) to remove bitterness.

In the same saucepan, combine 50g sugar and 50ml water. Bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves, creating a syrup. Add the blanched lemon peel strips to the syrup and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, or until the peel is translucent.
Carefully remove the peel from the syrup with a fork or tongs and place on parchment paper to dry completely. It will become slightly firm and shiny.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Mousse: Gently warm the heavy cream in a small saucepan with the two rosemary sprigs over low heat. Do not boil. Remove from heat and let the rosemary infuse for 15-20 minutes. Strain the cream, discarding the rosemary sprigs, and let it cool completely.

In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler), whisk together the egg yolks, 80g granulated sugar, lemon juice, and lemon zest. Whisk continuously for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens to a light custard consistency and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from heat.

Bloom the two gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes. Squeeze out excess water and stir the softened gelatin into the warm lemon custard until fully dissolved. Let the custard cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.

Once the rosemary-infused cream is completely chilled, whip it to soft peaks. Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled lemon custard in two additions until just combined, being careful not to deflate the mousse. Divide the mousse among 4 elegant serving glasses or small dessert bowls.
Chill the mousse in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until thoroughly set.

Prepare the Rosemary Sugar Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat. In a small bowl, whisk together the melted butter, 40g granulated sugar, flour, egg white, and finely chopped rosemary until smooth.

Drop small spoonfuls of the batter onto the prepared baking sheet, spreading them very thinly with the back of a spoon into desired shapes. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy around the edges. Remove from the oven and, if desired, quickly shape them over a rolling pin or small bowl while still warm and pliable to create curved tuiles. Let cool completely on a wire rack to crisp up. Store in an airtight container until serving.

Assembly and Serving: Just before serving, arrange the chilled Lemon-Rosemary Mousse in the center of the plate if serving deconstructed, or ensure it's beautifully presented in its glass. Artfully scatter the cold Sweet Chicken Essence Gelée cubes around and on top of the mousse. Garnish with the crispy Rosemary Sugar Tuiles and the translucent Candied Lemon Peel strips. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Symphonie mit Knuspriger Hähnchen-Essenz
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, ivory-hued panna cotta, smooth and glistening, sits elegantly in a delicate glass or on a minimalist white plate. It is adorned with vibrant yellow dots and artistic swirls of translucent lemon-rosemary gel. Scattered over and around the panna cotta are delicate, almost paper-thin shards of golden-brown crispy chicken skin, resembling caramelized tuiles, offering a surprising textural contrast. A few tiny, vibrant green rosemary micro-sprigs and delicate, curled lemon zest threads provide a final touch of fresh color and aroma, completing this sophisticated dessert.

ingredients.name: Fresh Rosemary Sprigs
ingredients.notes: about 10cm each, for panna cotta infusion

instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Lay the chicken skin flat between two sheets of parchment paper, then place a heavy oven-safe pan or another baking sheet on top to press it flat. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and extremely crisp. Remove from oven, drain on paper towels. While still warm, carefully separate and sprinkle evenly with 1 tsp fine granulated sugar and a pinch of sea salt. Allow to cool completely; it will become brittle. Break into small, delicate shards (about 1-2 cm).

Bloom gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes. In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, 80g sugar, lemon zest from 2 lemons, and the two 10cm rosemary sprigs. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture just begins to simmer (do not boil). Remove from heat, cover, and let infuse for 15 minutes. Remove rosemary sprigs. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into the warm cream mixture until fully dissolved. Stir in the 60ml fresh lemon juice. Divide the mixture evenly into 4 small serving glasses or molds. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until set.

In a small saucepan, combine 50ml fresh lemon juice, 50ml water, 30g sugar, and the small 5cm rosemary sprig. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and let infuse for 10 minutes. Remove rosemary sprig. Return mixture to low heat, whisk in agar-agar powder until fully dissolved (about 1-2 minutes). Pour the mixture into a shallow dish or small container and refrigerate until firm (about 30-60 minutes). Once set, carefully scoop the gel into a small food processor or use an immersion blender to blend until smooth and pipeable. Transfer to a piping bag (optional).

Carefully unmold the panna cottas (if using molds) onto serving plates, or serve directly in their glasses. Pipe or spoon small dots or swirls of the lemon-rosemary gel around the panna cotta. Arrange the crispy chicken skin shards delicately on top of and around the panna cotta. Garnish with a few fresh rosemary micro-sprigs and thin lemon zest curls. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Hähnchenschmalz-Sablé mit Gezuckerter Zitronencreme und Umami-Hähnchen-Knusper
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated fine-dining dessert plate features a vibrant yellow mound of smooth, glossy lemon cream at its center. Neatly arranged around or atop the cream are delicate, golden-brown circular sablé cookies, subtly flecked with green rosemary and lemon zest. A scattering of glistening, dark amber, finely crumbled 'Umami Chicken Skin Crisps' adds a surprising textural and savory contrast. The dish is garnished with a fresh, verdant sprig of rosemary and a thin, translucent slice of bright lemon, possibly with a few delicate edible flowers, creating an elegant and intriguing presentation.

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary
ingredients.notes: finely chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Chicken Fat (Schmaltz) and Umami Chicken Skin Crisps: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Carefully remove all skin from chicken. Cut the skin into small, uniform pieces (about 1x1 cm). Place chicken skin in a cold, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-low heat. Slowly render the fat, stirring occasionally, for 20-30 minutes until the skin pieces are golden brown and crispy. Strain the rendered fat (schmaltz) into a heatproof bowl; you should have approximately 80g. Reserve the crispy skin pieces. Increase oven temperature to 180°C (350°F). Toss the reserved crispy chicken skin pieces with 1 tsp granulated sugar, 1/4 tsp flaky sea salt, and 1/2 tsp very finely minced fresh rosemary. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 5-7 minutes until slightly caramelized and very crisp. Let cool completely, then finely chop or crumble them.

Make the Rosemary-Lemon Chicken Fat Sablé Dough: In a large bowl, whisk together 150g all-purpose flour, 50g powdered sugar, 1/4 tsp salt, zest of 1 lemon, and 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh rosemary. Add the 80g rendered chicken fat (schmaltz), ensuring it's chilled and solid but not rock hard. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to cut the fat into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gently bring the dough together to form a disc. Wrap in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

Bake the Sablés: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled sablé dough to about 3-4mm thickness. Use a small round or square cutter (about 4-5 cm diameter) to cut out sablés. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden. Let cool completely on a wire rack.

Prepare the Sweetened Lemon Cream: In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), whisk together the 3 large egg yolks, 70g granulated sugar, 80ml fresh lemon juice, and zest of 1 lemon. If desired for a very subtle hint, add a small sprig of rosemary to infuse (remove before chilling). Whisk continuously for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from heat. Gradually whisk in the 60g cold, cubed unsalted butter until fully incorporated and the cream is smooth and glossy. Strain the cream through a fine-mesh sieve for an extra smooth texture, if desired. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or until firm.

Assemble the Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of the chilled lemon cream onto each of 4 dessert plates. Arrange 2-3 sablé cookies elegantly on top or alongside the cream. Sprinkle the umami chicken skin crisps generously over and around the lemon cream. Garnish with a fresh sprig of rosemary, a thin lemon slice or segment, and optionally, a few edible flowers for a fine-dining presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosmarin-Zitronen-Wolke mit Goldschimmer
recipes.visual_description: Four elegantly plated desserts. Each plate features a pristine, pale yellow Rosemary-Lemon Mousse, either unmolded as a perfect cylinder or sphere, or served artfully in a small glass. The mousse has a delicate, airy texture. A glistening, clear lemon-rosemary glaze is artfully drizzled over and around the mousse, catching the light. Scattered around the mousse are irregular shards of golden-brown, translucent candied chicken skin crisps, reflecting a 'golden shimmer' and providing a striking textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant lemon segments are carefully placed alongside, adding a burst of color and freshness. A tiny, verdant sprig of fresh rosemary completes the garnish, offering an aromatic accent. The overall presentation is minimalist, sophisticated, and inviting, with a focus on clean lines and contrasting textures.

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Candied Chicken Skin Crisp: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lay the chicken skin flat between two sheets of parchment paper, then place a heavy baking tray on top to press it down. Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and very crispy. Remove from oven, blot excess fat with paper towels, and let cool slightly. Once cool enough to handle, but still pliable, cut into small, irregular shards.

While the chicken skin cools, prepare the candying syrup. In a small saucepan, combine 50g granulated sugar, 50ml water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly syrupy. Remove from heat.

Toss the crispy chicken skin shards in the warm sugar syrup until evenly coated. Spread them back onto a clean parchment-lined baking sheet. Return to the oven, reducing temperature to 150°C (300°F), and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until the syrup has caramelized and coated the skin crisps. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet; they will become very brittle. Break into smaller, bite-sized pieces if needed. Store in an airtight container.

Prepare the Rosemary-Lemon Mousse: In a small saucepan, gently warm 100ml of the heavy cream with the two small rosemary sprigs over low heat. Do not boil. Let it infuse for 10-15 minutes. Remove rosemary sprigs. Meanwhile, soak gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until soft (or prepare powdered gelatin according to package instructions).

Add 75g granulated sugar, 50ml fresh lemon juice, and 1 tsp lemon zest to the infused cream. Heat gently until the sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from the gelatin sheets (or add dissolved powdered gelatin) and stir into the warm cream mixture until fully dissolved. Let the mixture cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.

In a separate bowl, whip the remaining 200ml heavy cream until soft peaks form. Once the lemon-rosemary cream mixture has cooled to room temperature, gently fold it into the whipped cream until just combined. Be careful not to overmix.

Divide the mousse mixture into four small serving molds (e.g., small ramekins, dariole molds, or simply small glasses). Chill in the refrigerator for at least 3-4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Glaze: In a very small saucepan, combine 30ml fresh lemon juice, 30g granulated sugar, and one small rosemary sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until the mixture slightly thickens to a syrupy consistency. Remove from heat, discard rosemary sprig, and let cool to room temperature.

Assembly: Carefully unmold the Rosemary-Lemon Mousse onto individual serving plates (if using molds). If using glasses, serve directly. Drizzle each mousse with the cooled Lemon-Rosemary Glaze. Arrange a few pieces of the Candied Chicken Skin Crisp around or on top of the mousse. Garnish with fresh lemon segments and a small fresh rosemary sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Citrus-Rosemary Whisper: A Delicate Panna Cotta with Candied Chicken Lace
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, ivory-white panna cotta, softly set in an elegant glass, topped with a shimmering, translucent golden-yellow lemon-rosemary gelée. Delicately arranged on the gelée are intricate, almost ethereal shards of candied chicken lace, translucent and golden-amber, catching the light. Alongside, vibrant slivers of candied lemon peel add a bright citrus accent, and a tiny, verdant sprig of fresh rosemary provides a pop of color and aromatic contrast. The overall presentation is minimalist, refined, and speaks of understated elegance, with a surprising textural and flavor complexity.

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary sprigs
ingredients.notes: about 10cm each, for panna cotta infusion

ingredients.name: Small rosemary sprig
ingredients.notes: optional, for candied chicken lace syrup infusion

instructions.instruction: Prepare Candied Chicken Lace (Start the day before or several hours in advance): Slice the chicken breast extremely thinly against the grain, almost paper-thin. Aim for slices about 5x5 cm.

Make Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 100ml water, 50g granulated sugar, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and the small rosemary sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and let the rosemary infuse for 10 minutes, then remove the sprig.

Confit Chicken: Gently add the thin chicken slices to the warm syrup. Ensure they are submerged. Cover and let them poach very gently over low heat for about 5-7 minutes, until just cooked through and translucent. Do not boil vigorously.

Cool & Dehydrate: Carefully remove chicken slices from the syrup and place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Pat very dry with paper towels. Dehydrate at 60°C (140°F) for 4-6 hours in a dehydrator, or bake in a very low oven (80°C / 175°F) for 2-4 hours, propping the door slightly ajar, until completely dry and brittle. They should be translucent and crisp like 'lace'.
Store: Once cooled, break the candied chicken into small, delicate pieces or shards. Store in an airtight container until serving.

Prepare Lemon-Rosemary Panna Cotta: In a medium saucepan, combine heavy cream, milk, 80g granulated sugar, 2 rosemary sprigs, and lemon zest. Gently heat over medium-low heat until just simmering, stirring occasionally. Do not boil.
Steep: Remove from heat, cover, and let steep for 20-30 minutes to infuse the flavors.
Prepare Gelatin: While the cream steeps, soak the 3 gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.

Combine: Strain the cream mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, discarding rosemary and zest. Gently reheat the strained cream if it has cooled too much. Squeeze excess water from the softened gelatin sheets and whisk them into the warm cream until completely dissolved.
Chill: Divide the panna cotta mixture evenly into 4 serving glasses or ramekins. Refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.
Prepare Lemon-Rosemary Gelée: Soak 1 gelatin sheet in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.

Make Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml fresh lemon juice, 50ml water, 30g granulated sugar, and 1 small rosemary sprig. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and let steep for 10 minutes.
Combine: Strain the syrup, discarding rosemary. Squeeze excess water from the softened gelatin and whisk into the warm syrup until dissolved.

Chill: Allow the gelée mixture to cool slightly at room temperature. Once the panna cottas are fully set, carefully pour a thin layer of the cooled gelée mixture over each panna cotta. Refrigerate for another 1-2 hours until the gelée is set.
Assemble and Serve: Just before serving, carefully remove the panna cottas from the refrigerator.
Arrange: Garnish each panna cotta with delicate shards of the candied chicken lace, a few julienned pieces of candied lemon peel, and a small fresh rosemary sprig for aroma and visual appeal.
Serve: Serve chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Espresso & Cacao Braised Short Ribs with Parsnip Silk
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly plated fine-dining dish featuring a rich, dark brown braised beef short rib. The short rib is nestled atop a creamy, off-white parsnip puree, which forms a smooth, elegant base. A glossy, deep mahogany-colored sauce, thick and luxurious, is generously spooned over the short rib, creating an appealing sheen. The dish is garnished sparingly with vibrant green finely chopped chives or delicate microgreens, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is sophisticated and artful, with clear separation of components and a focus on texture and color contrast, against a minimalist white plate.

ingredients.name: Strong brewed coffee
ingredients.notes: or 2 shots espresso + water to make 1 cup

ingredients.name: Parsnips
ingredients.notes: about 1.5 lbs / 680g, peeled and roughly chopped

instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Pat the beef short ribs dry with paper towels. Season generously with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the short ribs on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Work in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pot. Remove seared ribs and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned. Add minced garlic and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour in the red wine, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to deglaze and release any browned bits. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the strong brewed coffee, beef broth, and unsweetened cocoa powder until the cocoa is fully dissolved. Add the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.

Carefully return the seared short ribs to the Dutch oven, ensuring they are mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot tightly with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the short ribs are fork-tender and easily pull away from the bone.

While the short ribs are braising, prepare the parsnip puree. Place chopped parsnips in a medium saucepan and cover with cold, salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the parsnips are very tender when pierced with a fork. Drain thoroughly.

Transfer the drained parsnips to a food processor or use an immersion blender. Add 1/2 cup heavy cream, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon white pepper. Blend until completely smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed. Keep warm, or gently reheat before serving.

Once short ribs are tender, carefully remove them from the pot and set aside on a warm plate, covered loosely with foil. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, pressing on the solids to extract all liquid; discard solids. Skim any excess fat from the surface of the sauce. Bring the sauce to a simmer over medium-high heat and reduce by about one-third to one-half, until it reaches a desired consistency (it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon), about 10-15 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the finely chopped bittersweet dark chocolate and 1 tablespoon unsalted butter until melted and smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of the warm parsnip silk onto the center of each plate. Place one braised short rib on top of the puree. Spoon the rich espresso and cacao sauce generously over the short rib. Garnish with chopped fresh chives or microgreens, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef & Caramelized Onion Braise
recipes.visual_description: A rich, rustic stew served in a deep ceramic bowl. Tender, dark brown beef chunks are nestled among deeply caramelized, golden-brown onion slices. The dish is coated in a glossy, dark brown, slightly thickened gravy, reflecting the light. A few fresh thyme sprigs or chopped parsley garnish the top, adding a touch of green. The overall presentation is warm, hearty, and inviting, suggesting comfort food.

instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Pat the beef cubes dry with paper towels. In a shallow dish, combine the flour, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper. Dredge the beef cubes in the flour mixture, shaking off any excess.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear the beef in batches until browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per batch. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove the seared beef and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the same pot. Add the sliced onions and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and tender, about 15-20 minutes. This slow cooking develops a rich sweetness.
Add the minced garlic and dried thyme to the pot with the onions. Cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to deglaze and loosen any browned bits. Bring the broth to a simmer.

Return the seared beef to the Dutch oven, along with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper. Stir to combine. Cover the pot tightly with a lid and transfer it to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender.

Once cooked, carefully remove the pot from the oven. Let the braise rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired, alongside mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Braised Beef & Caramelized Onion Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, cast-iron skillet filled with tender, glistening beef cubes bathed in a rich, dark brown, savory sauce. Deeply caramelized golden-brown onions are intertwined with the beef. The dish is garnished with bright green, freshly chopped parsley, adding a pop of color against the earthy tones of the beef and sauce. Steam gently rises, indicating its warmth, and the texture appears incredibly succulent and inviting.

instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Cut the beef chuck roast into 1.5-inch (4 cm) cubes. Pat the beef cubes dry with paper towels. Season them generously with 0.5 teaspoon of salt and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper. Dredge the seasoned beef in all-purpose flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the floured beef cubes in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan, until well browned on all sides, approximately 3-4 minutes per batch. Remove the seared beef from the skillet and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the same skillet. Thinly slice the 2 large yellow onions and add them to the skillet. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until the onions are deeply softened and caramelized to a rich golden brown color.
Mince the 3 cloves of garlic. Add the minced garlic and the 4 sprigs of fresh thyme (or 1 teaspoon dried thyme) to the caramelized onions. Cook for an additional 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour in the 2 cups of beef broth and 1 tablespoon of balsamic vinegar, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon to deglaze the pan. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Return the seared beef cubes to the skillet along with the 1 bay leaf. Add the remaining 0.5 teaspoon of salt and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper. Ensure the beef is mostly submerged in the liquid.

Cover the skillet tightly with a lid (or aluminum foil if your skillet does not have an oven-safe lid). Transfer the covered skillet to the preheated oven. Braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until the beef is incredibly fork-tender and easily pulls apart. Check periodically to ensure liquid doesn't evaporate too much; add a splash more broth if needed.

Carefully remove the skillet from the oven. Discard the bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Mince the 2 tablespoons of fresh parsley. Garnish the dish with the fresh chopped parsley before serving. Serve hot, directly from the skillet, perhaps over mashed potatoes or with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronenrosmarin Traum mit Knusperhähnchen
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, deconstructed dessert presented in an elegant clear glass or shallow bowl. A pale, creamy yellow lemon-rosemary mousse forms the base, its surface lightly swirled with a glistening, translucent lemon-rosemary syrup. Scattered around and atop the mousse are golden-brown, irregular shards of candied chicken skin, glistening with sugar and tiny flecks of rosemary, providing a striking textural contrast. A delicate, sandy-colored rosemary shortbread crumble is artfully sprinkled on the plate, adding another layer of texture. A fresh, vibrant green rosemary sprig stands upright as a garnish, possibly accompanied by a delicate edible flower, creating a visually intriguing and balanced composition.

instructions.instruction: Carefully remove any excess fat from the chicken skin and lay it flat between two sheets of parchment paper. Place another baking sheet on top to weigh it down.
Bake in a preheated oven until deeply golden brown and very crispy.

Remove from oven, blot excess fat with paper towels. While still warm, sprinkle evenly with 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt, 1 teaspoon lemon zest, and 1/4 teaspoon finely chopped fresh rosemary.
Let cool completely on a wire rack until brittle. Once cooled, break into small, irregular shards (approx. 1-2 cm). Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
In a medium bowl, combine 75g all-purpose flour, 25g powdered sugar, a pinch of fine sea salt, and 1/2 teaspoon finely chopped fresh rosemary.
Add 50g diced cold unsalted butter. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Spread the crumble evenly on a small baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake in a preheated oven until lightly golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes.

In a heatproof bowl set over a simmering saucepan of water (bain-marie), whisk together 100ml lemon juice, 2 tablespoons lemon zest, 80g granulated sugar, and 3 large egg yolks. Add the small rosemary sprig.
Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens to coat the back of a spoon and reaches 80°C (175°F). Do not boil.

Remove from heat, discard the rosemary sprig. Squeeze excess water from the bloomed gelatin and whisk it into the hot lemon mixture until fully dissolved. Let the mixture cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.

In a separate bowl, whip 200ml heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the cooled lemon mixture into the whipped cream, along with 1/2 teaspoon finely chopped fresh rosemary, until just combined.
Divide the mousse into 4 elegant serving glasses or small bowls. Chill in the refrigerator until set.
In a small saucepan, combine 50ml lemon juice, 50g granulated sugar, 50ml water, and the small rosemary sprig.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let it simmer to infuse the rosemary flavor.
Remove from heat, discard the rosemary sprig, and let the syrup cool completely.
Just before serving, drizzle a teaspoon of the Lemon-Rosemary Syrup over each chilled mousse.
Sprinkle a generous amount of the Rosemary Shortbread Crumble around the mousse.
Artfully place 3-4 pieces of the Candied Rosemary-Lemon Chicken Skin Crisps on top of or alongside each mousse.
Garnish with a small fresh rosemary sprig and edible flowers, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Hauch: Goldener Traum mit Knusprigem Akzent
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated fine-dining dessert. Four delicate, glistening white lemon-rosemary panna cottas, perfectly unmolded, stand elegantly on individual black slate or minimalist white ceramic plates. Each panna cotta is accompanied by a vibrant, glossy yellow quenelle of lemon curd, artfully placed beside it. A generous scattering of golden-brown, irregularly shaped, crispy chicken skin crumbles, infused with rosemary and a hint of sugar, is artfully sprinkled over the panna cotta and around the plate, creating a delightful textural contrast. The dish is garnished with a tiny, verdant fresh rosemary sprig and a glistening, translucent lemon segment, adding a final touch of freshness and color. The overall presentation is clean, modern, and inviting, with a focus on contrasting textures and a harmonious color palette of white, yellow, gold, and green.

ingredients.name: Chicken Skin
ingredients.notes: from about 2-3 chicken thighs, cleaned of excess fat

instructions.instruction: In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, 80g granulated sugar, and lemon zest. Add the 2 small rosemary sprigs. Heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer, stirring occasionally. Do not boil. Remove from heat and let infuse for 15 minutes.

If using gelatin sheets, soak them in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened. If using powdered gelatin, sprinkle it over 2 tablespoons of cold water in a small bowl and let it sit for 5 minutes to bloom.

Remove the rosemary sprigs from the infused cream. Squeeze excess water from the gelatin sheets (or microwave bloomed powdered gelatin for 10-15 seconds until dissolved) and stir into the warm cream mixture until completely dissolved. Stir in the 30ml fresh lemon juice.
Pour the panna cotta mixture evenly into 4 small molds or ramekins (about 150ml capacity each). Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.

In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler), whisk together the egg yolks, 50g granulated sugar, 60ml fresh lemon juice, and lemon zest. Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens to a custard consistency that coats the back of a spoon (about 8-10 minutes).

Remove the bowl from the heat. Add the cold, diced unsalted butter, one piece at a time, whisking vigorously until fully incorporated and the curd is smooth and glossy. Transfer the lemon curd to a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface to prevent a skin from forming, and chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Place the cleaned chicken skin on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the skin is golden brown and very crispy. Alternatively, you can render it in a dry skillet over medium-low heat until crispy, then drain excess fat.

Once crispy, remove the chicken skin from the oven/pan and immediately transfer it to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess fat. While still warm, finely chop or crumble the crispy skin. In a small bowl, toss the crumbled skin with 1 tbsp granulated sugar, 1/4 tsp fine sea salt, and 1/2 tsp finely minced fresh rosemary until evenly coated. Set aside.

To serve, carefully unmold each panna cotta onto individual dessert plates. If difficulty unmolding, briefly dip the bottom of the mold in warm water. Place a small quenelle or dollop of chilled lemon curd next to each panna cotta. Generously sprinkle the Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crumble over and around the panna cotta and curd. Garnish each plate with a small fresh rosemary sprig and a lemon segment. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Umami Mushroom & Caramelized Onion Skillet with Tangy Ginger Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and hearty skillet dish served in a shallow bowl or plate. The base features a rich, dark brown blend of deeply caramelized onions and golden-brown, earthy mushrooms. A vibrant, creamy swirl of bright white, tangy Greek yogurt is artfully drizzled over the savory mixture, creating a beautiful contrast. Hints of fresh green from chopped parsley or chives are sprinkled on top, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The overall presentation is warm, inviting, and full of texture.

instructions.instruction: In a large, heavy-bottomed skillet, add the diced beef fat. Cook over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the cracklings are crisp. Remove the cracklings with a slotted spoon (save for another use or discard). Increase heat to medium.

Add the thinly sliced onions to the rendered beef fat in the skillet. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until the onions are deeply golden brown and caramelized. Do not rush this step, as proper caramelization adds significant depth of flavor.
Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

Add the sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Increase the heat to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and are nicely browned and tender. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Pour in the vegetable broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes until the liquid has slightly reduced and thickened.

While the skillet simmers, prepare the yogurt. In a small bowl, whisk the plain full-fat Greek yogurt with a pinch of salt and pepper. If a thinner consistency is desired for drizzling, whisk in 1 teaspoon of water or lemon juice.

Divide the hot mushroom and onion mixture among 4 serving plates or bowls. Drizzle generously with the prepared tangy ginger-yogurt. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives before serving immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Savory Ginger-Mushroom Sauté and Tangy Yogurt Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: Four perfectly pan-seared, flaky white cod fillets, golden-brown and glistening from the beef fat, are arranged on individual rustic plates. Each fillet is generously topped with a vibrant, earthy sauté of caramelized yellow onions and browned cremini mushrooms, speckled with finely minced ginger. A creamy, bright white drizzle of tangy Greek yogurt artfully zigzags over the fish and sauté, adding a refreshing contrast. The dish is presented casually, inviting and wholesome, with the different textures and colors creating an appealing visual.

ingredients.name: Cod Fillets
ingredients.notes: about 6 oz (170g) each, skin on or off

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Tangy Yogurt Drizzle: In a small bowl, combine the plain Greek yogurt with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Stir well until smooth. Set aside in the refrigerator.
Prepare the Fish: Pat the cod fillets thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.

Sear the Fish: Heat 2 tablespoons of beef fat in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron works best) over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place the seasoned cod fillets, skin-side down if applicable, into the hot fat. Sear for 3-5 minutes per side, or until the fish is golden brown, crispy, and cooked through. The internal temperature should reach 145°F (63°C). Remove the fish from the skillet and set aside on a plate to keep warm.

Sauté the Aromatics and Mushrooms: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of beef fat to the same skillet (no need to clean it, the browned bits add flavor). Reduce heat to medium. Add the finely diced yellow onion and sauté, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 3-4 minutes.

Continue Sauté: Add the sliced cremini mushrooms to the skillet with the onions. Increase heat slightly to medium-high and sauté, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are tender and beautifully browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Finish Sauté: Stir in the finely minced fresh ginger and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant. Do not overcook the ginger to prevent bitterness.

Assemble and Serve: To serve, place one pan-seared cod fillet on each plate. Generously spoon the warm ginger-mushroom-onion sauté over the top of each fish fillet. Finish by drizzling a spoonful or two of the tangy yogurt over the sautéed vegetables and fish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tropical Gyu Don
recipes.visual_description: A steaming bowl of fluffy white short-grain rice, generously topped with glistening, thinly sliced beef and tender, caramelized onions bathed in a rich, sweet, and savory pineapple-infused sauce. The dish is vibrant, garnished with bright green slivers of fresh green onions and a small pop of crimson pickled red ginger, creating an inviting and colorful presentation typical of a Japanese beef bowl, but with a tropical twist.

ingredients.name: Beef, thinly sliced (e.g., ribeye or sirloin)
Dashi (Japanese soup stock)
ingredients.notes: or 1/2 cup water + 1/2 tsp dashi powder

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.notes: adjust to taste based on pineapple juice sweetness

instructions.instruction: Prepare the ingredients: Thinly slice the large yellow onion and set aside. If your beef is not already thinly sliced, slice it against the grain into very thin strips.

Prepare the sauce: In a medium bowl, whisk together the pineapple juice, soy sauce, mirin, sake, dashi (or water with dashi powder), granulated sugar, and grated fresh ginger until the sugar is dissolved. Set aside.
Cook the onions: Heat a large skillet or pot with a lid over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

Simmer the sauce: Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the softened onions. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and let it simmer for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

Cook the beef: Uncover the pot and raise the heat slightly to medium. Add the thinly sliced beef to the simmering sauce in a single layer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring gently, until the beef is just cooked through and no longer pink. Be careful not to overcook the beef.

Serve: Remove from heat. Ladle generous portions of hot steamed rice into individual serving bowls. Top the rice with the beef and onion mixture, ensuring plenty of sauce is included. Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions and a small mound of pickled red ginger, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Steaks with Caramelized Pineapple & Lemon Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A beautifully seared beef steak, sliced against the grain, revealing a juicy pink interior. It is artfully arranged on a rustic white plate, topped with golden-brown caramelized pineapple chunks. A glossy, slightly reduced lemon glaze shimmers over the beef and pineapple. A sprinkle of bright green fresh parsley and delicate lemon zest adds a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is vibrant and inviting, evoking a casual yet elegant dining experience.

ingredients.name: Fresh Pineapple
ingredients.notes: cored and cut into 1/2-inch thick rings or large chunks

instructions.instruction: Pat beef steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously on both sides with salt and black pepper.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef fat and olive oil. Once the fat has rendered and is shimmering, about 2-3 minutes.

Carefully place the seasoned beef steaks into the hot skillet. Sear for 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or adjust for desired doneness. Use a meat thermometer if preferred (130-135°F for medium-rare).
Remove the seared steaks from the skillet and transfer them to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest for at least 5-10 minutes. This is crucial for juicy steaks.

While steaks are resting, add the pineapple pieces to the same skillet, using the residual fat and drippings. Cook over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and slightly caramelized.

Add the minced garlic to the skillet with the pineapple and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Squeeze the juice from the large lemon directly into the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet (deglazing). Let it simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced.

Remove the pineapple from the pan and set aside. Slice the rested steaks against the grain into thick pieces. Arrange the sliced beef on serving plates. Spoon the caramelized pineapple and lemon glaze over the beef. Garnish with fresh lemon zest and chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cabbage & Noodle Stir-Fry with Pickled Jalapeño Kick
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, steaming bowl of stir-fried wide egg noodles mixed with tender-crisp green cabbage and browned cremini mushrooms. The dish is coated in a glossy, savory-tangy sauce. Bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds are scattered on top, with flashes of orange-red pickled jalapeño slices providing a pop of color and indicating a spicy kick. The overall impression is hearty, colorful, and appetizing.

ingredients.name: Pickled Jalapeño Slices
ingredients.notes: plus 2 tablespoons of the pickling brine

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: white and green parts separated and sliced

instructions.instruction: Cook the wide egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well, rinse with cold water to prevent sticking, and set aside.

In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, brown sugar, and vegetable broth (or water). If using, mix cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water to create a slurry, then whisk it into the sauce mixture.

Heat the neutral cooking oil in a large wok or a wide, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the white parts of the sliced scallions, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the sliced cremini mushrooms to the wok and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their moisture and start to brown. Add the thinly sliced cabbage and cook for 5-8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the cabbage is tender-crisp but still retains some bite.

Add the cooked noodles to the wok with the cabbage and mushrooms. Pour the prepared sauce over everything. Add the pickled jalapeño slices and 2 tablespoons of the pickling brine. Toss continuously for 2-3 minutes, ensuring all ingredients are well coated and heated through.
Transfer the Spicy Cabbage & Noodle Stir-Fry to serving bowls. Garnish with the green parts of the scallions, toasted sesame seeds, and fresh cilantro if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Cabbage and Butternut Squash Skillet with Green Peas
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and rustic dish presented in a deep, cast-iron skillet. Tender, golden-brown caramelized shredded cabbage is intertwined with bright orange, soft butternut squash cubes. Interspersed throughout are vibrant green peas, adding pops of color and freshness. A light sheen from the olive oil and broth coats the vegetables. A sprinkle of fresh green parsley garnishes the top, contrasting with the warm, earthy tones of the cooked vegetables. Steam gently rises from the comforting, savory dish.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: medium head, outer leaves removed, cored, and thinly shredded

ingredients.name: Butternut Squash
ingredients.notes: medium, peeled, deseeded, and diced into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes

instructions.instruction: Prepare all vegetables: Thinly shred the cabbage, dice the onion, peel and dice the butternut squash into 1-inch cubes, and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent.
Add the diced butternut squash to the skillet. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it begins to soften and lightly brown on the edges.
Stir in the shredded cabbage and minced garlic. Continue to cook for another 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the cabbage wilts significantly and starts to caramelize and turn golden-brown.

Pour in the vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the skillet and let it braise for 15-20 minutes, or until both the squash and cabbage are very tender.
Remove the lid and stir in the frozen green peas. Cook, uncovered, for 2-3 minutes until the peas are heated through and vibrant green.
Season the dish generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. If using, stir in the fresh chopped parsley just before serving.
Serve the Savory Cabbage and Butternut Squash Skillet hot as a hearty main course.

recipes.recipe_name: Toasted Candlenut Coconut Pudding with Gula Melaka Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: Four individual servings of a creamy, off-white coconut pudding, elegantly set in small, clear glass ramekins or artfully inverted onto white ceramic plates. Each pudding is generously adorned with a glistening, dark amber Gula Melaka (palm sugar) syrup, creating beautiful swirling patterns. A sprinkle of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes adds a delicate texture and visual contrast. The overall presentation is simple yet sophisticated, highlighting the natural, earthy tones of the ingredients. The dish appears smooth, rich, and inviting.

ingredients.name: Candlenuts
ingredients.notes: toasted and ground into a fine paste

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: plus 2 tablespoons cold water for slurry

instructions.instruction: Toast candlenuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Be careful not to burn them. Let cool, then grind them into a fine paste or powder using a food processor or mortar and pestle.

In a medium saucepan, combine full-fat coconut milk, 1 cup water, granulated sugar, salt, and the ground candlenut paste. If using, add the knotted pandan leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar dissolves.

In a small bowl, whisk 3 tablespoons cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of cold water until smooth. Gradually pour the cornstarch slurry into the simmering coconut mixture, whisking continuously. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until the pudding thickens to a custard-like consistency. Remove the pandan leaf (if used) and stir in vanilla extract.

Pour the hot pudding into 4 individual serving ramekins or a single large serving dish. Let it cool slightly at room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours, or until completely set and chilled.

While the pudding chills, combine chopped Gula Melaka (palm sugar) and 1/4 cup water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the palm sugar completely dissolves and the mixture forms a slightly thickened syrup. Let cool to room temperature.

Once the pudding is chilled and set, invert it onto serving plates (if using ramekins) or spoon directly from a large dish. Drizzle generously with the Gula Melaka syrup. Garnish with toasted coconut flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple-Hazelnut Glazed Chicken Thighs with Balsamic Roasted Brussels and Savory Quinoa
recipes.visual_description: A rustic yet elegant dish featuring four golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs glistening with a rich, dark maple-hazelnut balsamic glaze. They are nestled among deeply caramelized Brussels sprouts, some whole, some halved, with slightly charred edges. All components are artfully arranged over a fluffy bed of ivory quinoa, which provides a neutral contrast to the vibrant greens and browns. The glaze creates a beautiful sheen on the chicken and sprouts, hinting at the sweet, tangy, and nutty flavors. The overall presentation is warm and inviting.

instructions.instruction: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly under cold water. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa with 2 cups of water or chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.

Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Trim the ends of the Brussels sprouts and cut any larger ones in half. Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels and season lightly with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

In a medium bowl, whisk together the hazelnut butter, maple syrup, balsamic vinegar, olive oil, garlic powder, and red pepper flakes (if using) until smooth and well combined. This is your maple-hazelnut balsamic glaze.

On a large baking sheet, arrange the seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up. Add the trimmed Brussels sprouts around the chicken on the same baking sheet. Drizzle about half of the prepared glaze evenly over the chicken and Brussels sprouts. Toss the sprouts to ensure they are well coated.

Roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. After 20 minutes, remove the baking sheet from the oven. Brush the remaining glaze over the chicken thighs and toss the Brussels sprouts again to coat them evenly. Return to the oven and continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature reaches 165°F / 74°C) and the skin is crispy, and the Brussels sprouts are tender-crisp and caramelized.

Divide the cooked quinoa among four plates. Top each serving of quinoa with a glazed chicken thigh and a generous portion of roasted Brussels sprouts. Spoon any extra glaze from the baking sheet over the chicken and sprouts before serving warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Hazelnut Balsamic Glazed Chicken with Roasted Brussels & Quinoa
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic bowl featuring a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh glistening with a rich, dark hazelnut balsamic glaze. Alongside, a generous portion of fluffy, ivory quinoa provides a soft base, contrasted by the deep green and slightly charred edges of tender roasted Brussels sprouts. The dish is artfully arranged, promising a comforting yet sophisticated meal, perhaps garnished with a sprinkle of fresh green parsley and a few crunchy toasted hazelnut pieces.

instructions.instruction: Rinse quinoa under cold water. In a medium saucepan, combine 1 cup rinsed quinoa with 2 cups chicken broth (or water) and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). On a large baking sheet, toss the trimmed and halved Brussels sprouts with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Spread them in a single layer. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
While the Brussels sprouts are roasting, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season all over with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet (cast iron works well) over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken thighs and sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.

Transfer the skillet with the seared chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove chicken from the skillet and let rest on a cutting board for a few minutes.

While the chicken is resting, prepare the hazelnut balsamic glaze. In a small bowl, whisk together the hazelnut butter, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, and 2 tablespoons chicken broth (or water) until smooth. If the glaze is too thick, add a tiny bit more broth until it reaches a pourable consistency.

To serve, divide the cooked quinoa among 4 plates. Top each with a chicken thigh and a generous portion of roasted Brussels sprouts. Drizzle generously with the hazelnut balsamic glaze. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and chopped toasted hazelnuts, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and inviting skillet dish featuring golden-brown chicken pieces nestled among tender, browned mushrooms in a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. The dish is generously speckled with vibrant green fresh parsley, creating a warm and comforting appearance. It's presented in a cast-iron skillet, ready to be served.

instructions.instruction: Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Cut into 1-inch pieces. Season the chicken with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the same skillet. Add the diced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their liquid and start to brown. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Sprinkle the flour over the onion and mushroom mixture, stir well and cook for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

Reduce heat to low. Stir in the sour cream until fully incorporated. Return the cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir to coat the chicken and mushrooms in the creamy sauce. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes until everything is warmed through. Do not boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Taste and adjust seasoning with the remaining salt and pepper if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately, perhaps over rice or noodles.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Wolke mit Knuspriger Geflügelpraline
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated dessert presented on a minimalist white ceramic plate. In the center, a perfectly formed, ethereal cloud of pale yellow Lemon-Rosemary Mousse, airy and delicate. Around it, artistic swirls and dots of glistening, translucent Lemon-Rosemary Gel provide vibrant pops of yellow. Scattered elegantly are shards of golden-amber, irregularly shaped Crispy Candied Chicken Skin, offering a surprising textural contrast. A delicate drizzle of clear, aromatic Rosemary-Lemon Syrup traces subtle lines across the plate. The dish is garnished with tiny, fresh green rosemary micro-sprigs and perhaps a few vibrant edible flower petals, creating a refined and intriguing composition.

ingredients.name: Chicken skin
ingredients.notes: from 2-3 boneless, skin-on chicken breasts, cleaned of any meat/fat

ingredients.name: Gelatin sheets
ingredients.notes: approx. 4g total, or 1 tsp powdered gelatin

ingredients.name: Gelatin sheet
ingredients.notes: approx. 1g, or 1/4 tsp powdered gelatin, for gel

instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Place chicken skin, fat-side up, between two sheets of parchment paper and two baking sheets (to keep it flat).
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the skin is golden brown and most of the fat has rendered. Remove from oven, blot excess fat with paper towels.
Lightly sprinkle the skin with fine sea salt, then evenly coat with 2 tablespoons of granulated sugar.
Return to the oven for another 10-15 minutes, or until deeply golden and caramelized. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Remove from oven and immediately transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. Once cool, it will be very crisp. Break into irregular, bite-sized 'praline' pieces. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

In a small saucepan, gently heat 100ml of the heavy cream with 2 small rosemary sprigs until just simmering. Remove from heat, cover, and let steep for 15-20 minutes. Strain out rosemary, pressing to extract flavor, and let the infused cream cool.
Bloom the 2 gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes (or prepare 1 teaspoon powdered gelatin according to package directions).
In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), whisk together 2 egg yolks and 50g granulated sugar until pale and thick (sabayon consistency). Remove from heat.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into the warm sabayon until dissolved. Stir in 30ml lemon juice and 1 teaspoon lemon zest.
Gently fold the cooled infused cream into the sabayon mixture.
In a separate bowl, whip the remaining 100ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold the whipped cream into the sabayon mixture until fully combined and airy.
Pour the mousse into 4 individual serving glasses or molds (e.g., small ramekins or silicone molds). Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until set.
Bloom the 1/2 gelatin sheet in a bowl of cold water.

In a small saucepan, combine 60ml lemon juice, 70g granulated sugar, and 1 small rosemary sprig. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Add 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest. Remove from heat and let steep for 10 minutes. Strain out rosemary.
Return the liquid to the saucepan. In a separate bowl, whisk the 2 egg yolks. Slowly temper the warm lemon liquid into the egg yolks, whisking constantly.

Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a whisk or rubber spatula, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (approx. 3-5 minutes). Do not boil.

Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into the hot curd until dissolved. Add the 40g cold, cubed butter, one piece at a time, whisking until fully incorporated and smooth.

Strain the lemon curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl for extra smoothness. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface to prevent a skin from forming. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until set to a gel-like consistency.
In a small saucepan, combine 50ml water, 50g granulated sugar, 1 small rosemary sprig, and 1 lemon peel strip.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until sugar is dissolved. Remove from heat, cover, and let steep for 15 minutes.
Strain out rosemary and lemon peel. Let the syrup cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Carefully unmold the Lemon-Rosemary Mousse onto the center of 4 chilled dessert plates (if using molds) or serve directly in glasses.
Spoon or pipe small dots/quenelles of the Lemon-Rosemary Gel artistically around the mousse.
Arrange a few pieces of the Crispy Candied Chicken Skin 'praline' around the mousse.
Drizzle a small amount of the cooled Rosemary-Lemon Syrup over the plate.
Garnish with fresh rosemary micro-sprigs, small lemon segments, and edible flowers if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosmarin-Zitronen-Wolke mit Hähnchen-Crunch
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated dessert presented in an elegant, shallow bowl or on a minimalist white plate. At the center, a perfectly formed, pale yellow lemon-rosemary quark mousse, smooth and airy, perhaps unmolded into a delicate quenelle or a small cylindrical shape. Around the mousse, glistening, translucent cubes of bright yellow lemon gelée are artfully scattered, catching the light. Perched delicately on or beside the mousse are a few irregular, golden-brown pieces of crispy, sweet-glazed chicken skin tuiles, their shiny surfaces reflecting the light, providing a textural contrast. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary and perhaps a tiny, colorful edible flower (like a purple viola) complete the composition, adding a pop of color and natural elegance. The overall impression is light, fresh, and refined, with a subtle complexity.

instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F). Carefully remove skin from chicken thighs, scraping off any excess fat from the underside. Place chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper and press with a heavy oven-safe pan. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
Remove crispy chicken skin from oven and dab off any excess fat with a paper towel. Break into small, irregular 'tuile' pieces (approx. 2-3 cm).

For the sweet glaze, combine 2 tablespoons granulated sugar and 2 tablespoons water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 2 minutes until sugar dissolves and syrup slightly thickens. Add a tiny pinch of salt. Quickly toss the crispy chicken skin pieces in the hot syrup until lightly coated. Spread on a fresh sheet of parchment paper to cool and harden. They will become brittle and shiny.

For the Lemon Gelée, bloom 1 gelatin sheet in cold water for 5 minutes (or mix 0.5 tsp gelatin powder with 1 tablespoon cold water and let sit). In a small saucepan, combine 100ml lemon juice, 50ml water, and 30g granulated sugar. Heat gently until sugar dissolves; do not boil. Squeeze excess water from the gelatin sheet (or add bloomed powder) and stir into the warm lemon mixture until fully dissolved.

Pour the gelée mixture into a shallow dish (e.g., 20x10 cm) to a depth of about 0.5 cm. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours until fully set. Once set, cut into small, irregular cubes or use a small round cutter for elegant shapes.

For the Rosemary-Infused Cream, gently warm 50ml of the heavy cream in a small saucepan with 2 small fresh rosemary sprigs. Do not boil. Remove from heat, cover, and let steep for 15-20 minutes. Strain out the rosemary sprigs and let the infused cream cool completely.

For the Lemon-Rosemary Quark Mousse, bloom 2 gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. In a large bowl, whisk together 250g quark, 80g granulated sugar, 50ml lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon lemon zest until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the remaining 100ml heavy cream until soft peaks form.

Gently warm a small portion (about 2-3 tablespoons) of the quark mixture in a microwave or small saucepan. Squeeze excess water from the gelatin sheets and stir into the warm quark mixture until fully dissolved. Combine this warm gelatin-quark mixture with the main quark mixture. Stir in the cooled rosemary-infused cream.

Gently fold in the whipped cream until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Pour the mousse into 4 elegant dessert glasses or ramekins (or small molds for unmolding). Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until fully set.

To plate, carefully unmold the mousse onto individual dessert plates, or serve directly in the glasses. Arrange a few cubes or shapes of the lemon gelée around the mousse. Artfully place 2-3 pieces of the Crispy Sweet-Glazed Chicken Skin Tuiles on or around the mousse. Garnish with a small fresh rosemary sprig and edible flowers, if using. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Veggie Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and hearty skillet dish featuring tender, browned beef strips nestled among colorful, softened bell peppers (red and green), translucent onions, and earthy sliced mushrooms. The ingredients are coated in a rich, reddish-brown sauce infused with diced tomatoes and herbs. The dish is presented in a rustic cast-iron skillet, with a sprinkle of fresh green parsley providing a final pop of color. Steam gently rises, indicating its warmth and freshness.

ingredients.name: Bell Peppers
ingredients.notes: 1 red, 1 green, seeded and sliced into 1-inch strips

instructions.instruction: Pat beef strips dry with paper towels. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef in a single layer without overcrowding. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until nicely browned. Remove beef from skillet and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced bell peppers and sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables start to soften.

Stir in the undrained diced tomatoes, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, dried thyme, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Return the seared beef strips to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, cover, and let simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until beef is tender and flavors have melded.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley, if desired. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef and Tomato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic skillet dish featuring tender, rich brown beef cubes bathed in a thick, vibrant red tomato sauce. The sauce is flecked with translucent pieces of sautéed onion and minced garlic, with a subtle sheen from olive oil. The dish is presented in a deep, cast-iron skillet, garnished with a sprinkle of bright green fresh parsley, creating a comforting and appealing visual contrast.

instructions.instruction: Prepare ingredients: Cut the beef chuck into 1-inch cubes. Dice the yellow onion and mince the garlic cloves.

Brown the beef: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef cubes in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the browned beef and set aside.

Sauté aromatics: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the pot. Add the diced onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.

Combine and simmer: Return the browned beef to the pot. Add the undrained diced tomatoes, beef broth, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot to incorporate them into the sauce.

Cook until tender: Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the beef is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

Thicken and serve: For the last 15-20 minutes of cooking, uncover the pot if you desire a thicker sauce. Taste and adjust seasonings (salt, pepper) as needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley just before serving.
