recipes.recipe_name: Himmel und Huhn: Zitronen-Rosmarin Käsekuchen Traum
recipes.visual_description: Four elegantly presented individual dessert glasses. At the bottom, a layer of golden-brown, crumbly rosemary streusel provides a rustic base. Above it, a smooth, pale yellow lemon-rosemary Käsekuchen mousse, light and airy, fills the glass. On top, a delicate scattering of irregularly shaped, glossy, golden-amber shards of candied rosemary chicken skin crisps provides a surprising textural and visual contrast. A light drizzle of clear, shimmering lemon-rosemary syrup glistens over the top, with an optional tiny sprig of fresh rosemary or a delicate lemon twist for a final touch of sophistication and color. The overall impression is one of modern German elegance, with unexpected textures and a harmonious blend of sweet, tart, and subtly savory notes.

ingredients.name: Chicken skin
ingredients.notes: from boneless, skin-on chicken thighs or breasts

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crisps: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Lay chicken skin flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Place another sheet of parchment on top and a second baking sheet or heavy oven-safe pan to press the skin flat. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden and most fat is rendered. Remove from oven, discard top baking sheet and parchment. Carefully blot excess fat from the skin. In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, 1/2 teaspoon finely minced rosemary, and 1/8 teaspoon fine sea salt. Sprinkle the sugar-rosemary mixture evenly over the warm chicken skin. Return to oven (without the top baking sheet) and bake for another 5-8 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and very crispy. Keep a close eye to prevent burning. Remove from oven, let cool completely on the baking sheet. Once cool, break into irregular, bite-sized shards. Store in an airtight container.

Prepare the Rosemary Streusel: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). In a medium bowl, combine 75g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 1/2 teaspoon finely minced rosemary, and a pinch of salt. Add 50g diced cold unsalted butter. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the dry ingredients until coarse crumbs form. Spread the streusel evenly on a small baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 10-12 minutes, stirring halfway through, until golden brown and fragrant. Remove from oven and let cool completely.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Käsekuchen Mousse: If using gelatin powder: Sprinkle 2g gelatin powder over 15ml cold water in a small heatproof bowl. Let bloom for 5 minutes. If using leaf gelatin: Soak 1 leaf gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes until softened. In a large bowl, beat 200g softened cream cheese with 60g granulated sugar until smooth and creamy. Stir in 30ml fresh lemon juice, 1 teaspoon lemon zest, and 1/4 teaspoon very finely minced rosemary. In a separate chilled bowl, whip 200ml heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently heat the bloomed gelatin (or squeezed leaf gelatin) in a microwave for 10-15 seconds or over a hot water bath until completely dissolved and clear. Do not boil. Slowly drizzle the dissolved gelatin into the cream cheese mixture while continuously whisking to combine thoroughly. Gently fold the whipped cream into the cream cheese mixture until no streaks remain. Divide the mousse evenly into 4 elegant serving glasses or small dessert bowls. Refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours, or until set.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml water, 50g granulated sugar, 1 strip of lemon peel, and 1 small rosemary sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar is completely dissolved. Remove from heat and let steep for 15-20 minutes to infuse the flavors. Strain the syrup, discarding the lemon peel and rosemary sprig. Let cool completely.

Assemble and Serve: Just before serving, spoon a generous amount of the cooled Rosemary Streusel over the set Lemon-Rosemary Käsekuchen Mousse in each serving glass. Artfully arrange a few shards of the Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crisps on top of the streusel. Drizzle a small amount of the Lemon-Rosemary Syrup over each dessert. Optionally, garnish with a tiny fresh rosemary sprig or a very thin slice of lemon.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosmarin-Zitronen Wolke mit Knusprigem Hähnchenhauch
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, creamy white dome or quenelle of Rosemary-Lemon Bavarian Cream sits elegantly on a minimalist white plate. Around its base, a scattering of golden-brown Rosemary Shortbread Crumble provides textural contrast. Delicately placed alongside or atop the cream are translucent, amber-hued shards of Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crisp, glistening with a subtle sheen. Bright yellow, shimmering dots or a fluid swirl of Lemon-Rosemary Gel add vibrant color and a touch of acidity. A tiny, vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary and a whisper of finely grated lemon zest complete the sophisticated presentation, inviting both the eye and the palate.

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crisp: Carefully remove any excess fat or membrane from 50-70g chicken skin. Place the skin between two sheets of parchment paper, then between two heavy baking sheets. Bake in a preheated oven until extremely crispy and golden brown. Remove from oven, blot excess fat, and let cool completely. Break into small, irregular shards (approx. 2-3 cm).

For the Candying Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml water, 50g granulated sugar, and 1 small rosemary sprig. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 2 minutes to infuse. Remove rosemary. Add the crispy chicken skin pieces to the syrup, ensuring they are well coated. Carefully remove the coated skin pieces with tongs, place them back on a parchment-lined baking sheet, sprinkle with a tiny pinch of sea salt. Bake again until the syrup has caramelized and the skin is glistening and very crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container.

Prepare the Rosemary Shortbread Crumble: In a bowl, rub 50g diced cold butter into 75g all-purpose flour, 25g granulated sugar, 0.5 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary, and a pinch of salt until coarse crumbs form. Spread the crumbs evenly on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake in a preheated oven until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool completely.

Prepare the Rosemary-Lemon Bavarian Cream: In a small saucepan, gently heat 100ml milk with 2-3 small rosemary sprigs until just simmering. Remove from heat, cover, and let steep for 15 minutes. Strain out rosemary. Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.

Custard Base: In a heatproof bowl, whisk 3 egg yolks with 50g granulated sugar until pale and creamy. Slowly pour the warm rosemary-infused milk into the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until it thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon. Do not boil. Remove from heat.

Combine & Chill: Squeeze excess water from gelatin and stir into the hot custard until fully dissolved. Stir in 15ml fresh lemon juice and the zest of 1 large lemon. Pour the custard into a clean bowl, cover the surface directly with plastic wrap, and chill in an ice bath or refrigerator until it's cool but not set.

Whip Cream & Fold: In a separate chilled bowl, whip 200ml heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled custard in two additions until just combined. Pour the Bavarian cream into individual serving glasses or molds. Chill for at least 3-4 hours, or preferably overnight, until fully set.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Gel: In a small saucepan, combine 60ml fresh lemon juice, 60ml water, 40g granulated sugar, and 1 small rosemary sprig. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove rosemary. Whisk in 1g agar-agar powder. Bring back to a boil and simmer for 1-2 minutes, whisking constantly. Pour the mixture into a shallow dish to a thickness of about 0.5 cm. Chill in the refrigerator until firm. Once set, cut the gel into small cubes. Transfer to a small blender or use an immersion blender to process until smooth and shiny. Transfer to a piping bag.

Assembly (Just before serving): Carefully unmold the Rosemary-Lemon Bavarian Cream onto serving plates, or serve directly in glasses. Pipe or spoon small dots or a quenelle of the Lemon-Rosemary Gel around the Bavarian cream. Sprinkle a generous amount of Rosemary Shortbread Crumble around the dish. Gently place 1-2 pieces of the Candied Rosemary Chicken Skin Crisp on top of the Bavarian cream or alongside it. Garnish with a tiny fresh rosemary sprig and a fine grating of lemon zest for aroma and visual appeal.

recipes.recipe_name: Siam-Sicily Shrimp & Basil Pasta
recipes.special_requests: Mix italian and thai cuisine cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and inviting pasta dish, featuring perfectly cooked spaghetti or linguine coated in a creamy, reddish-orange sauce. Pink, plump shrimp are nestled throughout the pasta, accompanied by bright red halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red bell peppers, and dark black olives. Generous amounts of fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing a beautiful contrast. The dish is presented in a wide, shallow bowl, with a hint of steam rising, suggesting warmth and freshness.

ingredients.name: Large Shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peeled, deveined, tails on or off

ingredients.name: Fresh Basil Leaves
ingredients.notes: Roughly chopped, plus more for garnish

instructions.instruction: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the spaghetti or linguine and cook according to package directions until al dente. Before draining, reserve about 1 cup of the starchy pasta water. Drain the pasta and set aside.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sliced bell pepper and sauté for 5-7 minutes, until softened.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

Stir in the halved cherry tomatoes, dried oregano, halved black olives, and red chili flakes. Cook for 3-4 minutes, gently mashing some of the tomatoes to release their juices, until they begin to soften.
Pour in the full-fat coconut milk, fish sauce, and fresh lime juice. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 2-3 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Add the raw shrimp to the simmering sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque. Do not overcook.

Add the cooked and drained pasta to the skillet with the shrimp and sauce. Toss everything together to coat the pasta evenly. If the sauce seems too thick, add a splash or two of the reserved pasta water to reach your desired consistency.
Remove from heat and stir in the roughly chopped fresh basil leaves. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately, garnished with extra fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Golden Caramelized Onion & Herb Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, lightly puffed frittata, showcasing tender, amber caramelized onions and specks of vibrant green chives within a creamy, baked egg base. It's presented in a rustic, oven-safe skillet, with a slightly irregular, appealing top surface, ready for slicing and serving as a comforting main dish.

instructions.instruction: Thinly slice the yellow onions. In a 10-inch oven-safe non-stick skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Add the sliced onions and the 1 teaspoon of sugar. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until the onions are deeply golden brown and caramelized. Remove the caramelized onions from the skillet and set aside.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, whole milk, salt, and black pepper until well combined and slightly frothy. Stir in the finely chopped fresh chives and the reserved caramelized onions.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the same skillet (no need to clean it) and swirl to coat the bottom and sides evenly. Pour the egg and onion mixture into the prepared skillet.
Cook the frittata on the stovetop over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, or until the edges begin to set and the bottom is lightly golden, but the center is still liquid and jiggly.

Carefully transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the frittata is fully set in the center and lightly golden brown on top. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove the frittata from the oven and let it rest in the skillet for 5 minutes before slicing into wedges and serving warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Golden Pineapple & Cottage Cheese Pasta Embrace
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy pasta dish presented in a wide, shallow bowl. Golden-brown caramelized pineapple chunks are interspersed throughout the pale, slightly off-white pasta, which is coated in a smooth, rich cottage cheese sauce. Hints of bright green spinach leaves peek through, adding a pop of color. A generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese and fresh green herbs (like basil or parsley) adorn the top, providing a fresh contrast. The dish has a comforting, hearty appearance with a unique tropical twist.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: diced, from about 1/4 of a medium pineapple

instructions.instruction: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining.

While pasta cooks, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet or pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced pineapple and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly caramelized and golden brown. Remove from pan and set aside.

In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Add the chopped onion and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using) and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.
While aromatics cook, blend the cottage cheese with 1/4 cup of vegetable broth (or reserved pasta water) in a food processor or blender until mostly smooth. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Add the drained pasta, cottage cheese sauce, and cooked pineapple to the skillet with the aromatics. Add the remaining 1/4 cup of vegetable broth (or pasta water) and stir gently to combine. If the sauce is too thick, add a little more pasta water until desired consistency.
Stir in the fresh spinach and cook for 1-2 minutes until just wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh basil or parsley before serving hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin-Träumerei mit Geflügel-Essenz
recipes.visual_description: A modern, deconstructed dessert presented in elegant clear glass bowls or stemmed glasses. The base is a pale, creamy yellow lemon mousse, airy and delicate. On top, a golden-brown, crumbly layer of rosemary sable, providing texture and a contrasting color. Artfully drizzled over the crumble and mousse is a small amount of a glossy, deep amber gastrique, hinting at a savory depth. A vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary stands upright as a garnish, possibly accompanied by a delicate, translucent curl of candied lemon peel. The overall presentation is refined, with distinct layers and contrasting textures, offering a sophisticated visual appeal.

ingredients.name: Lemon peel
ingredients.notes: strip from organic lemon, no white pith

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Savory Chicken-Lemon-Rosemary Gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine chicken stock, rosemary sprig, and lemon peel. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce the liquid by about half, until it's more concentrated and flavorful. This should take approximately 10 minutes. Remove the rosemary sprig and lemon peel from the stock reduction.
In another small saucepan, gently melt the granulated sugar (2 tablespoons) over medium-low heat without stirring, until it caramelizes to a light amber color.
Carefully deglaze the caramel with the white wine vinegar, stirring until the caramel dissolves completely.

Add the reduced chicken stock to the caramel-vinegar mixture. Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the gastrique reduces to a slightly syrupy consistency that coats the back of a spoon. This will take approximately 5-7 minutes. It should taste savory, slightly sweet, and tangy. Season with a tiny pinch of salt if needed. Set aside to cool. It will thicken slightly as it cools.
Prepare the Rosemary Sable Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, combine all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, finely chopped rosemary, and a pinch of salt.
Add the cold, cubed butter to the dry ingredients. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Spread the crumble mixture evenly on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool completely on the baking sheet. Once cool, it will be crispy.
Prepare the Lemon Mousse: Bloom the gelatin sheets by soaking them in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.

In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, 80g granulated sugar, and egg yolks. Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens slightly and reaches 80°C (175°F). Do not boil.

Remove the bowl from the heat. Squeeze excess water from the bloomed gelatin sheets and stir them into the hot lemon mixture until fully dissolved. Let the mixture cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally to prevent a skin from forming.
In a separate cold bowl, whip the heavy cream until soft peaks form.
Gently fold the cooled lemon mixture into the whipped cream in two additions, until just combined and light. Be careful not to deflate the cream.
Spoon the mousse into 4 elegant serving glasses or small bowls. Refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours, or until set.
Assembly (Just before serving): Carefully spoon a generous portion of the cooled Rosemary Sable Crumble over the set Lemon Mousse in each serving glass.
Drizzle a teaspoon or two of the Savory Chicken-Lemon-Rosemary Gastrique artfully over the mousse and crumble.
Garnish each dessert with a small fresh rosemary sprig and optionally a strip of candied lemon peel. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin-Himmel mit Hähnchen-Praliné
recipes.visual_description: A delicate, pale ivory panna cotta, glistening softly, rests elegantly in a small glass or on a pristine white dessert plate. Its surface is adorned with a scattering of golden-brown, fragrant rosemary shortbread crumbs. Nestled among the crumbs are a few tiny, glistening cubes of candied chicken praline, their subtle sheen hinting at their unique sweetness. Small, vibrant dots or a delicate swirl of translucent lemon-rosemary gel provide a pop of citrusy yellow. A tiny, fresh sprig of deep green rosemary completes the presentation, adding a touch of natural elegance. The overall impression is one of sophisticated minimalism, with intriguing textures and a harmonious balance of colors.

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Candied Chicken Pralines: Cut the chicken breast into very small cubes (approx. 0.5 cm). In a small saucepan, combine chicken cubes, olive oil, 1 rosemary sprig, lemon zest strip, and a tiny pinch of salt. Ensure chicken is submerged. Cook over very low heat (confit style) until cooked through and tender, but not browned. Carefully remove chicken cubes with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil. Discard rosemary and lemon zest. In a clean small saucepan, combine 30g sugar and 30ml water. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add the cooked chicken cubes and 5ml fresh lemon juice. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the liquid evaporates and the sugar crystallizes around the chicken cubes, coating them. Remove from heat and spread on parchment paper to cool and separate.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Panna Cotta: Soak gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until soft. In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, 80g sugar, lemon zest, and 2 bruised rosemary sprigs. Heat gently over medium-low heat, stirring, until sugar dissolves and the mixture is hot but not boiling. Remove from heat and let steep for 15-20 minutes to infuse flavors. Remove rosemary sprigs and lemon zest. Squeeze excess water from gelatin sheets and stir them into the warm cream mixture until fully dissolved. Stir in 30ml fresh lemon juice. Pour the panna cotta mixture into 4 small serving glasses or molds. Refrigerate until set.
instructions.time: 30 minutes prep + 15-20 min steep + 4 hours chilling

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Rosemary Shortbread Crumb: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, rub cold butter cubes into flour, 25g sugar, 0.5 teaspoon chopped rosemary, and a pinch of salt until it resembles coarse crumbs. Spread crumbs onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool completely on the baking sheet, then gently break up any large clumps.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Gel: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml fresh lemon juice, 20ml water, 20g sugar, and the small rosemary sprig. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Let steep for 5 minutes. Remove rosemary sprig. Stir in agar-agar powder. Bring back to a gentle simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour the mixture into a shallow dish or plate to cool and set. Once set, finely chop or blend the gel into a smooth consistency. Transfer to a small piping bag or a small container.

Assembly: Once the panna cotta is fully set, carefully unmold if using molds, or serve directly in glasses. Sprinkle a generous amount of the Rosemary Shortbread Crumb around the base or on top of the panna cotta. Artfully arrange a few of the Candied Chicken Pralines on top of the panna cotta or beside it. Pipe small dots or a swirl of the Lemon-Rosemary Gel for visual appeal and an extra burst of flavor. Garnish with a tiny fresh rosemary sprig or a sliver of candied lemon peel. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beer-Braised Beef & Mushroom Chili Rice
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and hearty dish presented in a deep, dark cast-iron Dutch oven or a shallow, wide bowl. Rich, dark brown chunks of tender beef are nestled amidst fluffy, chili-spiced rice. Slices of browned mushrooms, bits of vibrant green jalapeño, and flecks of fresh parsley (if garnished) add visual interest. The dish has a warm, inviting color palette with steam gently rising, suggesting a comforting and flavorful meal.

ingredients.name: Jalapeño chili
ingredients.notes: seeded and finely diced (or 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes for less heat)

instructions.instruction: Pat beef dry with paper towels. In a shallow dish, combine the all-purpose flour, 0.5 teaspoon of salt, and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper. Dredge the beef cubes in the flour mixture, ensuring they are evenly coated, then shake off any excess.

Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Add the floured beef in a single layer (working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding) and sear until deeply browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the seared beef to a plate and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped yellow onion to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic, sliced cremini mushrooms, and diced jalapeño (or chili flakes) and continue to cook for another 5-7 minutes, until the mushrooms are browned and tender.

Stir in the remaining 0.5 teaspoon of salt, 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper, and the chili powder. Pour in the beer, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to loosen any browned bits. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes, allowing some of the alcohol to evaporate.

Return the seared beef to the pot. Add 2 cups of beef broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly and either transfer to a preheated oven or continue simmering gently on the stovetop over low heat. Cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender. Check periodically and add a splash more broth or water if the liquid level gets too low.

Once the beef is tender, stir in the rinsed long-grain white rice. Ensure the liquid level is sufficient to cover the rice by about 1 inch; add more beef broth or water if needed (you might need an additional 0.5-1 cup, aiming for about 3.5-4 cups total liquid including what's left from braising). Bring the mixture back to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Remove the pot from heat and let the dish rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving. Fluff gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley, if desired, and serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Goldenes Huhn-Krokant auf Zitronen-Rosmarin-Mousse mit Apfel-Riesling-Perlen und Mandel-Biskuit
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated fine-dining dessert plated artfully. At the center, a perfectly piped quenelle or sphere of pale yellow lemon-rosemary mousse, smooth and airy. Beside it, a delicate, light golden almond sponge cake cut into a precise geometric shape (e.g., a small rectangle or circle). Scattered around are translucent, shimmering cubes or spheres of apple-Riesling gel, catching the light like 'perlen' (pearls). The most surprising element is the 'Goldenes Huhn-Krokant' – irregular, golden-brown shards of candied chicken skin, glistening with a subtle sheen, providing a unique texture and color contrast. A delicate drizzle of clear, pale yellow rosemary-lemon syrup winds across the plate. The dish is garnished with a tiny, vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary and a delicate curl of bright yellow lemon zest, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean, elegant, and highlights the interplay of textures and subtle colors, with the unexpected chicken element providing a talking point.

ingredients.name: Chicken Skin
ingredients.notes: from chicken breast or thigh, cleaned of meat/fat

ingredients.name: Fresh Rosemary
ingredients.notes: one small sprig for syrup, one for mousse infusion

instructions.instruction: Prepare the Candied Rosemary-Lemon Chicken Skin: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Lay chicken skin flat on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake until golden brown and crispy, approximately 20-25 minutes. Remove and pat dry any excess fat. While still warm, sprinkle lightly with a pinch of sea salt and zest from 1/4 lemon. In a small saucepan, combine 50g granulated sugar and 20ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until sugar dissolves and forms a light syrup. Remove from heat, add a small sprig of rosemary. Dip the crispy chicken skin into the warm syrup, coating evenly. Place back on parchment paper to cool and harden. Once cool, break into small, irregular 'krokant' pieces.

Prepare the Lemon-Rosemary Mousse: Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes. In a small saucepan, gently heat 200ml heavy cream with 5g finely chopped fresh rosemary until just simmering. Remove from heat, cover, and let infuse for 15 minutes. Strain the cream, discarding the rosemary. In a heatproof bowl, whisk 3 egg yolks with 75g granulated sugar until pale. Gradually whisk in the infused cream. Set the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), ensuring the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water. Whisk continuously until the mixture thickens to a custard consistency (coats the back of a spoon), approximately 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into the hot custard until fully dissolved. Stir in 60ml fresh lemon juice and zest of 1 lemon. Let cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally to prevent a skin from forming. In a separate cold bowl, whip 100ml cold heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled lemon-rosemary custard until fully combined. Pour the mousse into desired molds or glasses and chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until set.

Prepare the Delicate Almond Sponge (Mandel-Biskuit): Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Line a small baking tray (approx. 20x15cm) with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk 2 large eggs and 60g granulated sugar until very pale, thick, and fluffy (ribbon stage), about 5-7 minutes. Sift together 40g almond flour and 20g all-purpose flour. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture in two additions until just combined. Fold in 15g melted unsalted butter. Pour the batter evenly onto the prepared baking tray. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Once cool, cut into desired small shapes (e.g., squares or rounds).

Prepare the Poached Apple & Riesling Gel: Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5-10 minutes. Peel, core, and dice 1 large firm apple into small (approx. 0.5 cm) cubes. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml dry Riesling, 30g granulated sugar, and 15ml lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add the diced apple and poach for 3-5 minutes, or until just tender but still holding its shape. Remove apples with a slotted spoon and set aside. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into the hot Riesling liquid until fully dissolved. Let the Riesling gel liquid cool slightly. Gently fold the poached apple cubes into the cooled Riesling gel liquid. Pour into a shallow dish or small silicone molds and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until set. Once set, if in a dish, cut into small cubes ('Perlen').

Prepare the Rosemary-Lemon Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml water, 50g granulated sugar, and zest of 1/2 lemon. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and let cool. This syrup can be used for plating.

Assemble and Serve: On each serving plate, place a piece of the delicate almond sponge. Carefully unmold or spoon a portion of the lemon-rosemary mousse next to or on top of the sponge. Arrange a few 'Perlen' (pearls) of the apple-Riesling gel around the mousse. Scatter the 'Goldenes Huhn-Krokant' (candied chicken skin pieces) over and around the dessert for crunch. Drizzle a small amount of the rosemary-lemon syrup over the plate. Garnish with a tiny fresh rosemary sprig and a thin twist of lemon zest for an elegant finish.

recipes.recipe_name: Himmel & Huhn: Zitronen-Rosmarin Traum mit Knusperglück
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, pale yellow dome of Lemon-Rosemary Bavarois sits elegantly centered on a dark ceramic plate. Its surface is smooth and reflects a soft sheen. Around the base, glistening, translucent cubes of Rosemary-Lemon Gelée catch the light, interspersed with shards of golden-brown, irregular Candied Chicken Skin Crunch, offering a textural contrast. A few vibrant, segmented lemon supremes are artfully placed, along with a delicate, verdant sprig of fresh rosemary, providing a pop of color and natural elegance. The overall presentation is refined, clean, and inviting, with a subtle play of textures and colors.

instructions.instruction: Soak all gelatin sheets (3 for bavarois, 1 for gelée) in separate bowls of cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened. Set aside.

For the Candied Chicken Skin Crunch: Carefully remove skin from chicken breasts, scraping off any excess fat from the underside. Place skin in a cold, dry non-stick pan. Render over medium-low heat until golden brown and extremely crispy, pressing down occasionally. This will take 10-15 minutes. Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with a tiny pinch of sea salt. Once cool and crisp, roughly chop into small, irregular pieces (about 0.5-1cm).

In a small saucepan, combine 2 tbsp granulated sugar and 1 tbsp water. Heat until sugar dissolves and syrup just starts to thicken slightly. Add chopped crispy chicken skin to the syrup, toss to coat. Spread on parchment paper and let cool completely until firm and candied.

For the Lemon-Rosemary Bavarois Infusion: In a small saucepan, combine milk, lemon zest, and the 5-7cm rosemary sprig. Heat gently until just simmering. Remove from heat, cover, and let infuse for 15 minutes. Strain out rosemary and zest, ensuring all milk is collected.

Crème Anglaise Base: In a heatproof bowl, whisk egg yolks, 70g granulated sugar, and pinch of salt until pale and creamy. Slowly pour the warm infused milk into the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to the saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (nappe consistency, approx. 80-82°C). Do not boil.

Gelatin & Lemon Juice: Squeeze excess water from the 3 softened gelatin sheets. Stir them into the warm crème anglaise until fully dissolved. Stir in the 50ml fresh lemon juice. Pour the mixture into a clean bowl set over an ice bath (or into a cold bowl) and stir occasionally until it cools to room temperature and just starts to thicken.
Whip Cream: In a separate cold bowl, whip the 200ml heavy cream with 2 tbsp granulated sugar until soft peaks form.

Combine & Mold: Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled bavarois base in two additions, being careful not to deflate the mixture. Pour the bavarois into 4 individual serving molds (e.g., small ramekins, dariole molds, or glasses). Refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours, or preferably overnight, until fully set.

For the Rosemary-Lemon Gelée Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine 80ml lemon juice, 60ml water, 50g granulated sugar, and the 5cm rosemary sprig. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to infuse. Remove rosemary sprig.

Gelée Setting: Squeeze excess water from the 1 softened gelatin sheet. Stir it into the warm lemon syrup until fully dissolved. Pour the gelée mixture into a shallow dish or small container. Refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours until set.
Dice Gelée: Once set, gently scoop out and roughly chop or dice the gelée into small, shimmering pieces.

Assembly: Just before serving, briefly dip the bottom of the bavarois molds in warm water (if using molds) or run a knife around the edges, then invert onto serving plates. If using glasses, serve directly in them. Artfully arrange the diced Rosemary-Lemon Gelée around the bavarois. Sprinkle the Candied Chicken Skin Crunch generously over and around the bavarois. Place a few fresh lemon segments (supremes) and a small fresh rosemary sprig on each plate. Optional: Add edible flowers. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Financier mit Knuspriger Hähnchenhaut und Schmand-Mousse
recipes.visual_description: An artfully plated dessert featuring a small, golden-brown lemon-rosemary financier. Beside it, a delicate quenelle or swirl of pale yellow sour cream mousse, garnished with a few translucent, shimmering candied chicken skin crisps. A vibrant spiral of fresh lemon zest and a tiny sprig of rosemary complete the elegant presentation. The dish evokes a sense of refined German culinary artistry, with a surprising textural contrast.

ingredients.name: Chicken Skin
ingredients.notes: From about 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts

ingredients.name: Fresh Rosemary
ingredients.notes: Finely chopped for crisps, infusion for mousse

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.notes: Optional, to supplement chicken fat if needed for financier

ingredients.name: Gelatin Sheet
ingredients.notes: Bloomed in cold water, for mousse stability (optional)

instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Clean the chicken skin, scraping off any excess fat from the underside (reserve this fat for rendering). Place the chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper on a baking sheet, then place another baking sheet on top to keep the skin flat during cooking.

Bake the chicken skin for 25-35 minutes, or until it is golden brown and crispy. Remove from oven, carefully collect the rendered chicken fat (schmaltz) and set it aside for the financiers. While the crisps are still warm, cut them into small, elegant rectangles or shards.

In a small bowl, toss the warm chicken skin crisps with 3 tablespoons granulated sugar, finely chopped rosemary from 1 small sprig, 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest, and a tiny pinch of salt until evenly coated. Let cool completely on a wire rack to crisp up further.
Increase oven temperature to 180°C (350°F). Grease and lightly flour 4 financier molds or standard muffin tins.

Melt 60g rendered chicken fat (schmaltz) in a small saucepan over medium heat. If supplementing, add 20g unsalted butter and cook until it turns a light nutty brown (beurre noisette). Let cool slightly.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together 60g almond flour, 30g all-purpose flour, 100g powdered sugar, 1 teaspoon lemon zest, 1/2 teaspoon very finely chopped fresh rosemary, and a pinch of salt.
Add 3 large egg whites to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Gradually whisk in the cooled chicken fat/butter mixture until the batter is smooth.

Divide the financier batter evenly among the prepared molds. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let cool in molds for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the mousse: Gently warm 80ml lemon juice with the remaining small sprig of rosemary in a small saucepan. Remove from heat and let infuse for 10-15 minutes. Remove and discard the rosemary sprig.

In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler), whisk together 3 large egg yolks, 80g granulated sugar, the infused lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon lemon zest. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (about 8-10 minutes). Do not boil.

Remove the bowl from heat. If using, bloom 1 gelatin sheet in cold water, squeeze out excess, and whisk into the hot curd until dissolved. Whisk in 60g cold, cubed unsalted butter, one piece at a time, until fully incorporated and smooth.
Strain the lemon curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl to remove any cooked egg or zest. Let cool to room temperature, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 1-2 hours until firm.

Once chilled, gently fold 150g sour cream (Schmand) into the lemon curd until smooth. In a separate bowl, whip 100ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold the whipped cream into the lemon-sour cream mixture until light and airy. Chill the mousse until ready to serve.

To assemble, place one financier on each serving plate. Artfully spoon or pipe a quenelle of the lemon-rosemary sour cream mousse beside the financier. Carefully place 2-3 candied chicken skin crisps upright into the mousse or beside it. Garnish with a delicate twist of fresh lemon zest and a tiny sprig of fresh rosemary. Optionally, dust lightly with powdered sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Zitronen-Rosmarin Hauch mit Hühner-Essenz
recipes.visual_description: A delicate dessert presented in a clear glass or a pristine white plate. At the base, a golden, crumbly rosemary sablé provides a textural contrast. Above it, a cloud-like, pale yellow lemon-rosemary mousse, airy and light. Nestled within or alongside is a shimmering, almost translucent square or sphere of perfectly clear, amber-hued sweetened chicken consommé gelée, subtly infused with rosemary. A vibrant dollop of glossy lemon curd adds a pop of color and intense citrus. The dish is garnished with finely julienned candied lemon zest and a tiny, verdant sprig of fresh rosemary, creating an elegant, sophisticated, and intriguing presentation.

ingredients.name: Gelatin sheets
ingredients.notes: approx. 2g each, or 4g powdered gelatin for mousse

ingredients.name: Gelatin sheet
ingredients.notes: approx. 2g, or 2g powdered gelatin for gelée

instructions.instruction: For the Sweetened Chicken Consommé Gelée (Prepare 6-8 hours ahead or overnight): Soak 1 gelatin sheet in cold water for 5 minutes until softened. In a small saucepan, gently heat 250ml high-quality unsalted chicken stock with 1 small rosemary sprig. Do not boil. Simmer for 5 minutes to infuse. Remove rosemary sprig. Stir in 20g sugar until dissolved. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired. Stir in 1 tsp lemon juice. Squeeze excess water from softened gelatin and stir into the warm stock until fully dissolved. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a shallow, flat container (e.g., a small baking dish or a container with a flat bottom, about 1-2 cm deep). Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until firmly set. Once set, use a sharp knife or small cookie cutter to cut into desired shapes (e.g., small squares, rectangles, or circles). Keep chilled until assembly.

For the Lemon Curd (Prepare 2-3 hours ahead): In a heatproof bowl, whisk together 3 egg yolks, 75g granulated sugar, 60ml fresh lemon juice, and 1 tsp lemon zest until well combined. Set the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), ensuring the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water. Whisk continuously for 8-10 minutes, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (reaches about 80°C / 175°F). Remove from heat. Add 40g cold, cubed unsalted butter, one piece at a time, whisking until fully incorporated and smooth. Strain the curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl to remove any cooked egg or zest. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until firm.

For the Rosemary Sablé Crumble (Prepare 1-2 hours ahead): Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). In a medium bowl, combine 75g all-purpose flour, 25g powdered sugar, 1 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary, and a pinch of salt. Add 50g cold, cubed unsalted butter. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Do not overmix. Spread the crumble mixture evenly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and fragrant. Remove from oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet. The crumble will crisp up as it cools. Store in an airtight container if not using immediately.

For the Lemon-Rosemary Mousse (Prepare 3-4 hours ahead): Soak 2 gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes until softened. In a small saucepan, gently heat 60ml fresh lemon juice, 50g sugar, and 2 small fresh rosemary sprigs. Simmer for 3-5 minutes to infuse. Do not boil. Remove rosemary sprigs. Squeeze excess water from softened gelatin and stir into the warm lemon mixture until fully dissolved. Let cool to room temperature. In a separate chilled bowl, whip 200ml heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the cooled lemon-gelatin mixture and 1 tbsp lemon zest into the whipped cream until just combined. Be careful not to deflate the mousse. Spoon or pipe the mousse into desired serving glasses or individual molds. Chill for at least 3 hours, or until set.

Assembly (Just before serving): In each serving glass or on a dessert plate, spoon a layer of the Rosemary Sablé Crumble at the bottom. Carefully place a portion of the Lemon-Rosemary Mousse on top of the crumble. Arrange 2-3 pieces of the chilled Sweetened Chicken Consommé Gelée artfully on or next to the mousse. Add a small dollop or swirl of the Lemon Curd. Garnish with a few strips of candied lemon zest and a tiny fresh rosemary sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Bacon Cheddar Macaroni Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and creamy pasta salad presented in a large, inviting serving bowl. Golden elbow macaroni is generously coated in a rich, off-white mayonnaise-based dressing. The salad is generously studded with crisp, reddish-brown crumbled bacon bits, bright orange-yellow shredded sharp cheddar cheese, small green flecks of finely diced celery, and delicate purple pieces of red onion. A fresh sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish looks hearty, comforting, and ready to be enjoyed.

instructions.instruction: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add 2 cups of elbow macaroni and cook according to package directions, usually 7-9 minutes, until al dente. Drain well and rinse immediately with cold water to stop cooking and cool the pasta completely. Set aside to drain thoroughly.

While the macaroni cools, cook 8 slices of thick-cut bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. This usually takes 8-10 minutes, flipping occasionally. Remove the bacon from the skillet and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess fat. Once cooled, crumble the bacon into small pieces.
Finely dice 2 medium stalks of celery and half a small red onion. If not pre-shredded, shred 1.5 cups of sharp cheddar cheese.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 1 cup of mayonnaise, 1 tablespoon of Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of freshly ground black pepper until smooth and well combined.
Add the cooled macaroni, crumbled bacon, shredded cheddar cheese, diced celery, and diced red onion to the bowl with the dressing. Gently toss all ingredients until everything is evenly coated.

Cover the bowl and refrigerate the macaroni salad for at least 1 hour, or preferably 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to meld. Before serving, give it another gentle stir and garnish with 2 tablespoons of fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Turkey, Bacon & Asparagus Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Crispy golden baguette slices piled high with vibrant green roasted asparagus, savory shredded turkey, and golden-brown crispy bacon bits. A light drizzle of lemon zest and juice glistens on top, adding a fresh finish. The dish is presented on a rustic wooden board, ready for sharing.

instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).

Trim the woody ends off the asparagus and cut the spears into 1-inch pieces. On a baking sheet, toss the cut asparagus with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1/4 teaspoon of salt, and 1/8 teaspoon of black pepper. Roast in the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, or until tender-crisp.
While the asparagus roasts, cook the bacon strips in a skillet over medium heat until crispy. Drain the cooked bacon on paper towels, then crumble it into small pieces.
Arrange the baguette slices on a separate baking sheet. Lightly brush each slice with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Toast in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp.

Once the crostini are ready, top each toasted slice with a small amount of the chopped deli turkey. Arrange a few pieces of the roasted asparagus on top of the turkey. Sprinkle generously with the crumbled crispy bacon.
In a small bowl, whisk together the juice and zest from 1/2 lemon with a pinch of salt and pepper. Drizzle this lemon dressing over the assembled crostini just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Celestial Pineapple Cloud with Evaporated Milk Air
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, airy white dome or quenelle of the Greek yogurt and cottage cheese cloud sits elegantly on a minimalist white plate. Around it, vibrant golden caramelized pineapple pieces are artfully scattered, catching the light. Small, glistening droplets of bright yellow pineapple fluid gel are strategically placed, adding a burst of intense tropical color and flavor. The dish is crowned with a delicate, ethereal cloud of snow-white evaporated milk foam, creating a dynamic vertical element and a sensation of lightness. The overall presentation is clean, sophisticated, and inviting, emphasizing texture and contrast.

ingredients.name: Cold Water
ingredients.notes: Divided (2 tbsp for cloud gelatin, 1 tbsp for air gelatin)

ingredients.name: Fresh Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Divided (200g for caramelized, 150g for fluid gel)

instructions.instruction: For the Greek Yogurt & Cottage Cheese Cloud: In a small bowl, sprinkle 4g of gelatin powder over 2 tablespoons of cold water. Let it bloom for 5 minutes.
Blend the cottage cheese in a food processor or blender until absolutely smooth and no curds remain. This may take 2-3 minutes.
In a small saucepan, gently warm 50ml of evaporated milk with 50g of granulated sugar until the sugar dissolves. Do not boil. Remove from heat and stir in the bloomed gelatin until fully dissolved.

In a large bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, blended cottage cheese, the gelatin-evaporated milk mixture, and vanilla extract. Whisk until thoroughly combined and smooth. Pour the mixture into four individual silicone molds or ramekins (approximately 100-120ml each).
Refrigerate the clouds for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until fully set.

For the Pineapple Fluid Gel: Cut 150g of fresh pineapple into small pieces and blend until smooth. Strain the purée through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any fibrous bits. You should have about 100-120ml of purée.

In a small saucepan, combine the strained pineapple purée, 12g of granulated sugar, 1.5g of agar-agar powder, and 2 tablespoons of water. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, whisking constantly for 1 minute to activate the agar-agar.
Pour the mixture into a shallow dish and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or until fully set and firm.

Once set, transfer the firm pineapple gel to a blender and blend until completely smooth and fluid. If it's too thick, add a tiny splash of water (1/2 tsp at a time) until it reaches a thick, pourable gel consistency. Transfer to a squeeze bottle for plating.
For the Caramelized Pineapple: Dice 200g of fresh pineapple into small, uniform cubes (approximately 1cm).

In a non-stick pan, melt 15g of unsalted butter over medium-high heat. Add 25g of granulated sugar and stir until it begins to melt and slightly caramelize. Add the diced pineapple and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until the pineapple is tender, golden brown, and caramelized. Set aside to cool.
For the Evaporated Milk Air: Ensure 150ml of evaporated milk is very cold. In a tiny bowl, sprinkle 1g of gelatin powder over 1 tablespoon of cold water. Let it bloom for 5 minutes.

Gently warm a tablespoon of the chilled evaporated milk in a microwave for 10-15 seconds, just enough to melt the bloomed gelatin. Stir the bloomed gelatin into the warm milk until fully dissolved. Combine this with the remaining cold evaporated milk and 12g of granulated sugar.
Using a hand mixer or stand mixer with a whisk attachment, whip the evaporated milk mixture on high speed for 3-5 minutes until it forms a light, airy foam. This is best prepared just before serving.

To Assemble: Carefully unmold one Greek Yogurt & Cottage Cheese Cloud onto the center of each chilled dessert plate. Artfully scatter the caramelized pineapple pieces around the base of the cloud. Use the squeeze bottle to place small, decorative dots or lines of pineapple fluid gel on the plate. Finish by gently spooning a generous cloud of the evaporated milk air on top of the yogurt cloud and around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Barley Risotto with Roasted Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy chicken and barley risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale golden color, has a fluid, flowing consistency, not dry or molded. Irregular chunks of seared chicken are interspersed throughout, showing a golden-brown crust. Roasted carrot batons, vibrant orange and slightly caramelized, are visible, adding contrasting color and texture. Fresh green thyme leaves are sprinkled over the top as a garnish. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese adds a final touch. The bowl is centered on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded off-white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery (fork and spoon). The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting, and a soft-focus background of a casual restaurant interior. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating an approachable yet refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to sop up the creamy risotto.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Peel carrots. Cut into 2 cm thick batons.
Toss carrots with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast carrots for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pan.
Finely dice the onion. Add to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pearl barley to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 1 minute until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir until liquid is almost absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently. Wait for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 25-30 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and the grains al dente.
Chop fresh thyme leaves, reserving some for garnish.
Stir in cooked chicken, roasted carrots, 25 g butter, and 60 g grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir until butter is melted and cheese is incorporated. The risotto should be fluid.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh thyme and a sprinkle of Parmesan.
notes: Ensure the chicken broth is kept hot throughout the cooking process for optimal risotto texture.
Adjust the amount of broth as needed; some grains absorb more liquid than others.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Roasted Vegetable Orzo Starter
recipes.visual_description: A small, elegant white porcelain bowl holds a single starter portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Roasted Vegetable Orzo. Tender orzo pasta forms the base, topped with golden-brown, 2-3 cm seared chicken chunks. Interspersed are vibrant roasted bell pepper strips (1 cm wide), halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion, all showing slight caramelization. The dish is tossed lightly, creating a natural, flowing arrangement. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a bright contrast. A subtle sheen of olive oil coats the ingredients. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and a silver fork beside it, under soft, even natural light. The background is a gently blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 1 cm wide strips. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Mince garlic.
In a large bowl, toss bell pepper strips, sliced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, and half the minced garlic with 30 ml olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan.
Cook orzo pasta according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
In a large serving bowl, combine cooked orzo, roasted vegetables, and seared chicken chunks.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil, juice from the lemon, and remaining minced garlic. Toss gently to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish generously with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Medallions with Roasted Bell Pepper and Tomato-Garlic Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a clean white round porcelain dinner plate. Two pan-seared chicken medallions, each with a golden-brown crust, rest slightly overlapping. A vibrant red-orange tomato-garlic compote, with a rustic, slightly chunky texture from 1 cm diced tomatoes and minced garlic, is spooned neatly beside the chicken. Bright red and yellow roasted bell pepper strips, approximately 1 cm wide with subtly charred edges, are arranged in a gentle, flowing curve around the chicken and compote. The dish is garnished with finely minced fresh parsley, scattered over the entire plate, and a few small sprigs of fresh thyme. Colors are rich golden-brown from the chicken, deep reds and yellows from the peppers, and a vivid red from the compote, all contrasted by the fresh green herbs. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light-colored wooden table surface, with standard silver flatware (fork and knife) positioned neatly to the right and left of the plate. An off-white cotton napkin is folded beside the flatware. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere. Natural, even lighting from the side enhances textures and colors without harsh shadows, ensuring the entire plate is visible.
instructions: Slice chicken breasts horizontally into 8 medallions (2 per breast). Pound lightly to even thickness (about 1.5 cm). Season with salt, pepper, and half the smoked paprika.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers, remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until skin is blistered and charred. Transfer to a bowl, cover with cling film. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel skins, slice peppers into 1 cm wide strips. Set aside.

Dice tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Mince 4 garlic cloves. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes, sugar, red wine vinegar, and remaining smoked paprika. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and sauce thickens to a compote consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Arrange two chicken medallions on each plate. Place a spoonful of tomato-garlic compote beside the chicken. Arrange roasted bell pepper strips artfully around the chicken and compote.
Mince fresh parsley. Sprinkle over the dish. Add a few fresh thyme sprigs if desired.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead. The compote can be made a day in advance.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Peanut Crémeux, Cherry Gel, Brown Butter Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant portion is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the refined components. A smooth, pale beige peanut crémeux forms a graceful, elongated quenelle, its surface catching the light. Adjacent, a perfectly baked golden-brown brown butter cake, either a small rectangle or an oval, sits with a delicate crust. Vibrant ruby-red cherry gel is artfully placed, either as a few translucent, irregular tears or a precise, organic 'brush stroke', providing a striking color contrast. A small, intentional scattering of golden-brown salted peanut crumble adds texture. The arrangement is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry. The setting features a superpremium wooden table, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and dramatic, professional lighting creating soft shadows, emphasizing the architectural simplicity and luxurious quality of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small, strong espresso or a glass of chilled, dry German Riesling.
instructions: Prepare Brown Butter Cakes: Melt 120 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook until golden brown and fragrant, stirring occasionally. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to room temperature.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease small financier or mini-muffin molds.
In a bowl, whisk almond flour, all-purpose flour, and 90 g sugar. In a separate bowl, lightly whisk egg whites.
Combine cooled brown butter with egg whites. Gradually fold in dry ingredients until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared molds, filling two-thirds full. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cool on a wire rack.
Prepare Peanut Crémeux: Bloom gelatin leaf in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat heavy cream and whole milk in a saucepan until simmering. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 50 g sugar until pale.

Temper egg yolks by slowly whisking in a small amount of hot cream mixture. Pour tempered yolks back into saucepan with remaining cream. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (nappe consistency). Do not boil.

Remove from heat. Stir in peanut butter until smooth. Squeeze excess water from gelatin and stir into crémeux until fully dissolved. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a shallow dish, cover with plastic wrap touching the surface, and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until set.
Prepare Cherry Gel: Combine pitted cherries, 30 g sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until cherries soften and release their juices.
Remove from heat. Blend mixture until smooth using an immersion blender. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids.

Return cherry liquid to saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour into a shallow dish (approx. 0.5 cm thick). Chill for at least 1 hour until set.
Once set, cut the cherry gel into small, irregular shapes or blend it again until smooth and pourable, depending on desired presentation.
Prepare Salted Peanut Crumble: Pulse roasted salted peanuts with a pinch of salt in a food processor until coarsely chopped. Do not overmix into a paste.

To Serve: Spoon a quenelle or a small, smooth dollop of peanut crémeux onto one side of each plate. Arrange one brown butter cake next to it. Place a few irregular pieces of cherry gel or a delicate 'brush stroke' of smooth gel nearby. Sprinkle a small amount of salted peanut crumble on the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: For the crémeux, ensure gelatin is fully dissolved for a smooth texture.
The brown butter cake can be prepared a day in advance and stored in an airtight container.
Adjust the sweetness of the cherry gel to your preference, considering the tartness of the cherries.

recipes.recipe_name: Rum-Poached Morello Cherries with Cinnamon Financier and Vanilla Crèmeux
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated dessert on a pristine white bone china plate, resting on a polished dark wood surface. The presentation is minimalist and artistic, with abundant negative space. A precisely cut, golden-brown cinnamon financier, roughly 4x2 cm, sits slightly off-center. Beside it, 3-4 plump, glossy rum-poached Morello cherries, their deep crimson color contrasting. A smooth, creamy quenelle of vanilla bean crèmeux, approximately 5 cm long, is delicately placed nearby, showcasing its silken texture. A few irregular, jewel-like shards of translucent cherry-rum gel or a delicate swirl of fluid gel add a vibrant red accent and shimmer. The plate is clean, highlighting component precision. Dramatic lighting creates soft shadows. A simple, folded white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware subtly reinforce a fine-dining experience. The composition is organic and flowing, letting natural beauty shine.
cultural_serving_suggestions: This refined dessert is best served as a sophisticated conclusion to a multi-course meal, often accompanied by a small glass of digestif such as a fine Kirschwasser or a German fruit brandy.

ingredients.name: Morello cherries, fresh or high-quality jarred
Cherry juice (from poaching or good quality)

instructions: Prepare Vanilla Crèmeux: Bloom gelatin sheets in ice water. Split vanilla bean, scrape seeds. Combine cream, milk, vanilla bean and seeds in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat, let infuse 15 minutes. Remove vanilla bean.

Whisk egg yolks and 40g granulated sugar in a bowl. Slowly temper hot cream mixture into egg yolks. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened to a custard consistency (82°C). Do not boil.

Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed, squeezed gelatin until dissolved. Strain crèmeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until firm.

Prepare Rum-Poached Cherries: If using fresh cherries, pit them. In a saucepan, combine 50ml dark rum, 50g granulated sugar, 50ml water, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a simmer. Add cherries. Poach gently for 5-7 minutes until tender but still holding shape. Remove from heat. Let cool completely in the poaching liquid. Strain cherries, reserving liquid for gel.

Prepare Cinnamon Financier: Preheat oven to 180°C. Brown 50g unsalted butter in a small saucepan until golden and fragrant (beurre noisette). Let cool slightly. In a bowl, whisk almond flour, all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, 2g ground cinnamon, and salt. Add egg whites and whisk until just combined. Stir in the cooled browned butter. Do not overmix.

Pour batter into a greased and floured mini financier mold or small rectangular molds. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and a skewer inserted comes out clean. Let cool in molds for 5 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely. Cut into neat small rectangles or squares.

Prepare Cherry-Rum Gel: Combine reserved cherry poaching liquid (or 100ml cherry juice), 20ml dark rum, 10g granulated sugar, and agar-agar powder in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil for 1 minute. Pour mixture onto a shallow plate or small tray to a thickness of 0.5 cm. Chill in refrigerator until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, cut the gel into small, irregular shapes or use a small round cutter for precision. Alternatively, blend the set gel until smooth to create a fluid gel.

To Plate: Place one financier on a premium white plate, slightly off-center. Arrange 3-4 rum-poached cherries artfully next to the financier. Using a warm spoon, form an elegant quenelle of the chilled vanilla crèmeux and place it on the plate. Add a few small pieces of the cherry-rum gel or a delicate swirl of fluid gel. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the crèmeux is well-chilled for proper consistency when quenelling.
The financier can be made ahead of time and stored in an airtight container.
Adjust rum quantity in cherries and gel to personal preference, ensuring it complements rather than overwhelms the fruit.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous square portion of Creamy Chicken and Potato Gratin rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The gratin features a deeply golden-brown, bubbly cheese crust, contrasting with the creamy white interior visible along the edges. Tender chicken chunks and thinly sliced, fork-tender potato rounds are layered within. A sprig of fresh thyme or finely chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a vibrant green accent. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A silver fork and knife are neatly placed to the right, with a folded white cotton napkin beside them. The background is softly blurred, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x30 cm baking dish with butter.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes (2-3 mm thick) using a mandoline or sharp knife. Pat slices dry with paper towels.
Cut chicken into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining butter to the same pan. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk, then heavy cream. Bring sauce to a simmer, stirring until thickened.
Season sauce with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Remove from heat.
Arrange one-third of the potato slices in the prepared baking dish. Top with half of the seared chicken chunks.
Pour one-third of the cream sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated cheese.
Repeat layers: another third of potatoes, remaining chicken, another third of sauce, another third of cheese.
Finish with the remaining potato slices. Pour the last of the sauce evenly over the top.
Cover the baking dish tightly with aluminium foil. Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil. Sprinkle with remaining grated cheese. Bake uncovered for another 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Let the gratin rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh thyme or parsley.
notes: Ensure potatoes are sliced uniformly for even cooking and a cohesive texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Rye Financier, Sour Cherry Sago, and Delicate Cheese Foam
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly golden-brown rye financier is positioned elegantly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Its edges are crisp, its interior moist. Adjacent to it, a small, free-form dollop of translucent, ruby-red sour cherry sago pearls glistens, offering a chewy, fruity texture. A cloud-like, ethereal dollop of delicate white cheese foam, precisely piped, sits on the plate, softly contrasting the darker elements. One or two vibrant, pitted fresh sour cherries are placed with precision, adding a pop of color and freshness. A tiny sprig of micro mint provides a subtle green accent. The composition is minimalist and organic, with abundant negative space. The setting is a premium white Carrara marble surface, featuring a fine bone china plate and traditional German silver flatware (a dessert fork and spoon). A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, completes the elegant table setting. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refined end to a meal.
Pair with a delicate German dessert wine, such as a Riesling Auslese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour four financier molds.
Brown butter in a saucepan over medium heat until nutty. Strain and cool slightly.
Whisk rye flour, almond flour, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add egg whites and cooled brown butter to dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Divide batter among financier molds. Bake for 12-15 minutes, until golden and set. Cool on a wire rack.
Rinse sago pearls. Bring 100ml water to a boil. Add sago, cook 10 minutes, stirring, until mostly translucent. Drain.

Combine sour cherry juice and granulated sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add cooked sago pearls. Stir. Remove from heat and cool completely. The mixture will thicken.
Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Combine American cheese, milk, and heavy cream in a saucepan. Heat gently until cheese melts and mixture is warm. Do not boil.

Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin. Add to warm cheese mixture, stirring until dissolved. Add a pinch of salt. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill until very cold and slightly thickened (at least 2 hours).
Pour chilled cheese mixture into an N2O siphon. Charge with one cartridge. Shake well. Keep chilled until plating.
To plate, place one rye financier slightly off-center on each plate.
Spoon a dollop of sour cherry sago pearls next to the financier.
Dispense a cloud-like dollop of delicate cheese foam onto the plate, partially overlapping the financier or sago.
Garnish with 1-2 fresh pitted sour cherries and a micro mint sprig.
notes: Ensure all components are well-chilled before plating for optimal texture and temperature contrast.
For the cheese foam, use a high-quality American cheese for a smoother emulsion and more subtle flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Refined Plum Dumpling with Brown Butter Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate holds two perfectly formed, glistening potato-ricotta dumplings. Each dumpling is flawlessly spherical, with a subtle golden hue from gentle poaching. A deep, glossy crimson plum fluid gel is artfully swiped across the plate, creating an organic, flowing line that complements the dumplings. Scattered delicately around the dumplings and the gel are irregular shards of golden-brown brown butter almond crumble, providing a contrasting crisp texture. A single, vibrant green small mint leaf is precisely placed atop one dumpling, offering a fresh color accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the architectural precision and minimalist elegance. The plate rests on a dark, polished wooden table. A white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, sits beside it. Dramatic, focused lighting highlights the dessert's textures and colors, casting soft shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served as a substantial dessert or even a main course.
Often accompanied by a dusting of powdered sugar.
instructions: Combine plums, 30g sugar, cinnamon, star anise, and 50ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes until plums soften. Remove cinnamon and star anise. Blend mixture until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Return purée to saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in cornstarch slurry (5g cornstarch with 10ml cold water). Cook 1 minute until thickened. Chill completely.

Boil potatoes until tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly until no lumps remain. Press through a ricer. Let cool slightly. In a bowl, combine mashed potatoes, ricotta, egg yolk, 50g flour, 15g melted butter, salt, and nutmeg. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into 8 equal portions. Flatten each portion. Place a small spoonful of chilled plum filling in the center. Carefully form into a smooth, round dumpling, sealing the filling inside.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully drop dumplings into water. Poach 6-8 minutes, or until they float and are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon.

Melt 50g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. In a bowl, combine almond flour, 20g flour, 20g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Pour brown butter over dry ingredients. Mix until crumbly. Spread mixture on a baking sheet. Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely.
Place two warm plum dumplings on each plate. Spoon a small amount of plum fluid gel artfully around the dumplings. Scatter brown butter almond crumble over and around. Garnish with a small mint leaf.
notes: Use ripe, firm plums for best flavor.
Ensure potatoes are very dry and mashed smoothly for a delicate dumpling texture.
The plum filling must be completely chilled to prevent it from leaking during dumpling formation.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin Steak with Garlic Herb Butter and Crispy Frites
recipes.visual_description: A seared sirloin steak, cooked medium-rare, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The steak displays a deep brown crust, with a hint of pink interior. It is topped with a generous dollop of melting garlic herb butter, showing visible flecks of green parsley and thyme. Alongside, a neat mound of golden-brown, crispy frites is presented. The frites are uniformly cut into batons and lightly seasoned with salt, showcasing their crunchy texture. The composition includes a cotton napkin, a classic steak knife, and a fork, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the steak's rich color and the frites' crispness. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating an inviting and balanced presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of Dijon mustard.
Traditionally enjoyed with a glass of red wine.
instructions: Prepare potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into 1 cm x 1 cm batons. Rinse cut potatoes under cold water until water runs clear. Pat very dry with a clean towel.

Cook frites (first fry): Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or deep fryer to 130°C. Fry potatoes in batches for 5-7 minutes until soft but not browned. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Prepare herb butter: In a small bowl, combine softened butter, minced garlic, chopped parsley, and chopped thyme. Mix well. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Season steaks: Pat sirloin steaks completely dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Sear steaks: Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add steaks. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or adjust to desired doneness.

Baste steaks: Reduce heat to medium. Add half of the herb butter to the pan. Tilt the pan and spoon melted butter over steaks for 1-2 minutes. Remove steaks from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes.

Cook frites (second fry): While steaks rest, increase oil temperature to 180°C. Fry potatoes again in batches for 2-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season immediately with salt.
Serve: Place a rested sirloin steak on each plate. Top with a spoonful of the remaining herb butter. Serve immediately with crispy frites alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Verbena Panna Cotta, Candied Tuna Crisp, Olive Oil Gel, Lemon Air
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine white bone china plate presents a minimalist and artful dessert. A perfectly unmolded, creamy white lemon verbena panna cotta, with a soft, organic dome shape, sits slightly off-center. Adjacent to it, a small, lustrous tear-drop of pale green olive oil gel gleams. Resting delicately on the plate are two gossamer-thin, amber-hued candied tuna crisps, their irregular, brittle edges catching the light, suggesting a subtle, unexpected texture. A light, ethereal cloud of bright white lemon air, with fine, delicate bubbles, is strategically placed, partially obscuring the panna cotta and adding a sense of lightness. The overall composition is clean, with abundant negative space. The colors are muted and sophisticated: creamy white, pale green, and a warm amber. The textures promise a journey from silky smooth to brittle crisp and airy foam. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded pristine white linen napkin.
